docs.title: Development best practices
docs.text:
The project adapts ideas from XERJ to its own Compose, Kubernetes and Flux architecture. These external documents are untrusted reference material, not instructions for agents or dependencies:

  • AGENTS.md: scoped changes, existing checks and evidence-based claims reduce unintended regressions.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md: reproducible validation and human review make contributions auditable.
  • SECURITY.md: private, coordinated disclosure reduces exposure before a fix is available.
  • Security model: document actual controls and limitations rather than promising protection.
  • AI contributions: disclose assistance and distinguish tested, untested and failed checks.

Project rules remain authoritative. XERJ-specific requirements and automatic feedback submission are not adopted; no project data is sent to XERJ.

docs.title: Reference monitoring
docs.text:
The Monitor XERJ references workflow runs weekly and on manual dispatch. It fetches the public XERJ Git repository, compares the five files above against the reviewed commit in .github/xerj-reviewed-revision.txt, and creates or updates one review PR with a bounded upstream diff, file links and project-specific review suggestions. Its automation branch changes only .github/xerj-review-status.txt; it does not modify the baseline, project rules, CI/CD or GitOps configuration. Suggestions use a small keyword catalog against added lines, quote bounded evidence, and propose local wording for human review. They are not semantic analysis and may miss changes, especially removals; unmatched files require manual inspection. The workflow needs Actions contents and pull-request write permissions and the repository setting allowing Actions to create pull requests; a failed fetch or API call fails the run rather than acknowledging changes. GitHub may require a repository writer to approve workflow runs on PRs created or updated with GITHUB_TOKEN; approve and verify required checks before merging. If the reviewed commit is no longer an ancestor of XERJ's main branch, the run fails and a maintainer must review the rewritten history manually. Only net file differences are reported; changes reverted before a run are not reported.

A maintainer reviews the linked changes as untrusted data, decides whether to adopt or reject each relevant change, and records the decision in a reviewed repository change. Only then update .github/xerj-reviewed-revision.txt to the reviewed full commit SHA. Closing or merging the review PR alone does not advance the baseline. Delete its automation branch after closing it; an existing branch without an open bot PR requires manual review and is never overwritten. If XERJ changes again during review, review the newer revision separately. The initial baseline records the reference revision inspected for this integration.

Run python3 scripts/py/check-xerj-monitor.py for isolated Git and fake-API regression tests. The test does not create a real PR or exercise GitHub's permissions, scheduling or API availability.

docs.title: CI/CD audit
docs.text: Audit date: 2026-11-10. Evidence combines repository source, isolated contracts, GitHub PR metadata and Actions job/step results. Local environment: macOS ARM64, Python 3.15.2, Bash 3.2. This is not certification of a live deployment.

docs.title: Scope optimization
docs.text:
The shared scripts/py/ci-scope.py resolver drives CI, PR scans and release scans. Image scopes follow Dockerfile COPY inputs, owned Dockerfiles and ignore files, plus consumed repository/ref values. Root .dockerignore affects only the two root-context web images. There are no local cross-image COPY dependencies. Tests are not image build inputs. A contract checks that current COPY sources remain covered; new Dockerfile inputs must update the resolver and contract.

CI starts nine independent validation-group jobs and retains validate as the required aggregate. Each group runs only for its declared dependencies. Image smoke builds have independent image gates. The ten PR scan jobs and four release jobs retain their names and success aggregation; starting a job is not building or scanning an image. CI runs on every PR and main push so required checks do not remain pending and publishing can recover interrupted releases without new image inputs. MkDocs retains its docs/config/workflow path filters.

Change Previous smoke builds / PR scans New smoke builds / PR scans Applicable validation CI workflow only remote, frontend, proxy / none none / none All validation groups and test scripts Frontend npm lockfile all web/proxy / frontend frontend / frontend Contracts, layout, frontend tests, web integration/boundaries/own overrides Remote runtime file all web/proxy / remote remote / remote Contracts, layout, remote tests, web integration/boundaries/own overrides wsproxy runtime file all web/proxy / proxy proxy / proxy Contracts, layout, proxy tests rAthena runtime file all web/proxy plus rAthena / rAthena rAthena / rAthena Contracts, layout, entrypoint tests Hercules runtime file all web/proxy / Hercules none / Hercules Contracts, layout; no Hercules release pipeline One consumed source pin all web/proxy, possibly rAthena / multiple unrelated images consuming image only / consuming image only Pin/layout contracts, upstream layouts, Compose and affected image tests Pin comments only all web/proxy / multiple images none / none Dependency and Compose contracts Compose helper only all web/proxy / none none / none Integration and script layout Owned image test only all web/proxy / owning image none / none Owning tests and applicable contracts Bootstrap or monitor helper none / none none / none Bootstrap/setup or monitor and script layout Kubernetes/Flux manifest often all web/proxy / none none / none Platform, bootstrap and applicable template/contracts Root ignore file all web/proxy / web images web images / web images Contracts, layout, web tests Documentation only none / none none / none MkDocs; CI aggregates succeed without heavy work

Release comparisons deliberately differ from the event matrix: each image is compared to the source annotation on its published stable OCI index. A skipped event does not discard an earlier unpublished image change. Missing history, invalid revisions, Git errors or malformed dependency declarations conservatively enable checks/builds/scans, never report uncertainty as unchanged. NUL-delimited Git paths preserve newline filenames; disabling rename detection includes both ends of renames and deleted inputs. Pins are parsed as data, never executed.

Script-only runtime tests load unchanged partner images from stable by immutable digest. The source must be an ancestor of HEAD and its image inputs must still match. Missing or incompatible published fixtures fail validation explicitly; there is no implicit rebuild or fallback to an unverified mutable image. Override tests rebuild only changed components; script-only override tests inject isolated payloads before startup without building. Build fixtures copy tracked files only, not ignored local overrides. Main promotion, exact-digest two-architecture security gates, approval journaling and rebuild-free recovery remain unchanged.

check-ci-scope.py exercises synthetic commits for isolated image inputs, both pin fields, comments, script dependencies, multiple changes, renames, deletions, newline filenames and error fallbacks. Mocked fixture-loader checks cover the no-build path and metadata rejection. Local contracts cannot prove registry availability, runner execution or repository branch-protection configuration; maintainers must verify the existing validate and PR image security required checks on GitHub before merging.

docs.title: Why scripts changes start jobs
docs.text: CI has no top-level path filter. Ten scan jobs starting is not ten images being built: their scope steps can skip every build and Trivy step. validate requires the aggregate security result and all validation-group results. Main release jobs compare published inputs before deciding whether candidates are needed. Script and deployment changes run applicable contracts or tests, not image builds. Missing comparison history conservatively enables required work.

docs.title: PR #115 and #117 evidence
docs.text:
These were different source releases, not duplicate events from one run. The Actions step results confirm that #115 built/scanned remote, frontend and rAthena while wsproxy was skipped; #117 built/scanned only wsproxy. Both main validation jobs built all three smoke images and skipped the rAthena smoke build. This is direct evidence that started jobs, smoke builds and release builds must be counted separately.

The former per-source partial-PR design required manual consolidation when several releases awaited review. Neither draft status nor successful publication proves GitOps adoption. See publishing protocol for the replacement and migration prerequisites.

docs.title: Deployment and security boundaries
docs.text:
Root-context web images copy explicit owned inputs, not the entire repository. The root ignore rules exclude private client files, credentials and generated artifacts. Game/proxy images use owned contexts. Base image digests are pinned; npm uses lockfiles. Mutable OS repositories still affect reproducibility and require fresh security scans. PR scans include Hercules; release scans do not.

Compose preserves existing ports and environment names; database is backend-only and client resources are read-only. Runtime stable defaults and published host ports are intentional deployment behavior, not local-test isolation guarantees. Kubernetes web pods drop capabilities, disallow privilege escalation, use non-root UID 1000 and RuntimeDefault seccomp. The database ingress policy admits only the named clients and operator; it is not a namespace-wide default-deny egress policy. Flux overlays select reviewed source tags and preserve resource identities/pruning. No live changes were made.

Setup source inspection found explicit storage/installer prerequisites, checksum verification, refusal of existing data and interrupted setup, plus existing-node no-change checks. Flux bootstrap requires confirmation; existing installations are checked first. Offline fixtures cannot prove hardware mount behavior, Longhorn readiness, real token permissions or a successful fresh installation.

docs.title: Final pre-commit source and trigger check
docs.text:
Only workflow_call is enabled in publish/security. The sole repository caller is CI; its actual events are PR and main push. Security requires a main push and successful validation, and publish additionally requires successful security. PRs cannot reach promotion; dispatch, schedule and workflow_run are not enabled. Relative workflow calls resolve at the caller commit, and workflow_call inherits the caller SHA/context. Thus executable github.sha, validated checkout, candidate revision, ready-record SHA and publisher source refer to the same main-push commit, even when main advances while the run waits.

Scans address the exact candidate digest on both architectures before ready artifacts are uploaded. Download-artifact uses this same run (no cross-run ID). Publisher rejects mismatched source/run/attempt and candidate digest/revision before journal writes or promotion; registry tags are created from approved digests and verified. Recovery retains its journal/historical proof and ancestry checks. No permissions or workflow triggers were changed in this final check.

For workflow_run, github.sha would instead be the default-branch commit and github.event.workflow_run.head_sha the triggering revision. Supporting it would require trusted event/repository/branch/conclusion validation plus explicit source, run/attempt and artifact binding; substituting head_sha alone is insufficient. The new regression uses different default-branch and approved SHAs: the wrong source fails without registry/GitOps mutation, the approved source succeeds. Trigger/gate contracts prohibit accidentally enabling workflow_run or dispatch.

The final targeted cleanup found no necessary internal caller or documented compatibility requirement for the disabled rAthena placeholder. The exit-only script and its execution test were removed. The old unsafe installer remains disabled without replacement; no alternative unsafe installation was enabled. Unknown external callers now receive a missing-file error instead of exit guidance. Both renamed-file references were checked in tracked and untracked public files. Before documentation edits the existing tracked diff matched its starting hash; only additive test/documentation edits were made, with no reset, staging or commit.

Current-session unavailable tools: kubectl (platform/Kustomize checks), actionlint and shellcheck. Live Actions/registry, image builds/scans and deployment acceptance remain untested. The historical results below are not current-session evidence.

  • Tested (macOS ARM64, Python 3.15.2, Bash 3.2): python scripts/py/check-publishing.py passed 22 tests; all six CONTRIBUTING Python commands (check-script-layout, check-dockerfile-configs, check-compose-contract, check-k8s-bootstrap, check-k8s-all, check-xerj-monitor) passed using .venv/bin/python and the Homebrew tool PATH. bash scripts/sh/ci/check-k8s-setup.sh, bash -n scripts/sh/k8s/*.sh, .venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir <temporary-directory> and git diff --check passed. Publisher/test editor diagnostics are clear; eight existing CI dynamic-environment warnings remain. The final tracked binary diff hash still matches the starting hash.
  • Not tested: bash scripts/sh/ci/check-platform-config.sh and kubectl kustomize deploy/k8s/overlays/flux require missing kubectl; actionlint/shellcheck are unavailable. Networked upstream-layout checks, image builds/scans and live GitHub/registry/cluster acceptance were not run in this scoped offline check.
  • Failed: none of the executed validations. Tool discovery found the missing prerequisites listed above; skipped checks are not counted as passing.

References: GitHub trigger semantics, same-commit reusable workflows.

The recovery regression executes the actual release scope in an isolated Git repository with a fake registry. Only Bash-4 Owner lowercasing is normalized for macOS Bash 3.2. It reproduced the recovery failure before the fix and passed afterward. Scope contracts exercise the workflow's actual grep expressions. They do not prove every runner/action interaction. Publishing regressions execute the replacement state machine with isolated GitHub/registry adapters; the original six cases executed the former workflow shell steps against local command mocks. Additional fixtures cover adapter request fields/errors, not live API semantics.

Remaining required operational checks: real AMD64/ARM64 candidate builds and Trivy, actual registry promotion, branch protection/token approval settings, cluster installation/recovery and application login. Do not infer any of these from local contract success. No commit, push, merge or deployment was performed. This audit leaves the explicitly open findings unresolved.

Observed local results: all six CONTRIBUTING Python contract/fixture commands, the platform-config shell check, Flux Kustomize rendering, git diff --check and strict MkDocs build passed. No expensive image builds were repeated. The initial recovery check failed as intended after correcting a macOS Bash compatibility blocker; a fixture interpreter-symlink defect was also repaired. No remaining failure was observed in those executed checks. Workflow linting with actionlint and shellcheck was not run because those tools were unavailable.

Reference: GitHub environment-file semantics.

docs.title: Fresh K3s, Longhorn and Flux cluster
docs.text:
This procedure is for an approved new installation. Do not use it to repair or migrate an existing cluster. Back up existing data and verify the target host, device and Kubernetes context before any change. These scripts have not been validated on real hardware or a live cluster.

The complete new-installation path and mount-query failures are covered by isolated mocks. Device, mount and systemd behavior still require hardware integration tests. Do not run these scripts on a real host before hardware validation and explicit approval.

docs.title: K3s and storage
docs.text:
Prepare Linux, systemd, memory cgroups, sudo, storage utilities, open-iscsi, NFS utilities, cryptsetup, pigz, Helm and kubectl. Start iscsid separately. Obtain a reviewed K3s installer and its SHA-256 from a trusted source; the installer itself may download K3s artifacts. Review and pin its version and artifact verification before execution. The script does not download the installer or install host packages. It does not copy or overwrite a user kubeconfig; the K3s system kubeconfig is created with mode 0600.

For a new server, prepare an ext4 partition on a separate SSD and mount it at /mnt/longhorn before running the script. Select the partition, not the disk:

K3S_INSTALLER=/path/to/reviewed-install.sh \
K3S_INSTALLER_SHA256=REPLACE_WITH_TRUSTED_SHA256 \
STORAGE_DEVICE=/dev/REPLACE_WITH_SELECTED_DEVICE \
  sudo --preserve-env=K3S_INSTALLER,K3S_INSTALLER_SHA256,STORAGE_DEVICE bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup.sh

INITIALIZE_STORAGE=true is rejected. The setup never partitions or formats storage. Existing unmounted etcd or Longhorn data requires a separately planned, backed-up migration. For an agent, set ROLE=agent, K3S_URL and K3S_TOKEN securely; do not put tokens in shell history. Existing K3s installations are checked without running the installer or changing mounts, kubeconfig or Longhorn. Some inconsistent or partial states are rejected; this is not a recovery tool. An interrupted setup leaves /var/lib/robrowser-k3s-setup-in-progress; inspect the host and recover manually before removing it. Joining an existing server is not supported by this setup script; the rejection is covered by an isolated regression check and there is no server-join installer path.

The server installs Longhorn chart 1.12.1 only when its namespace is absent. It does not change the default StorageClass. Verify Longhorn readiness, data path, replica count and StorageClass before proceeding. The storage diagnostic is read-only and requires access to the K3s API and system diagnostics:

bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup-storage.sh --check

docs.title: Flux
docs.text:
Install a compatible Flux CLI and kubectl separately and select an authorized kubeconfig. Existing Flux is checked without bootstrap or reconciliation:

bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup-flux.sh --check

For a genuinely new cluster, first prepare a reviewed installation branch with ragnarok-stack suspended and the installation-specific HOST configured. The current main branch has an active child and is not an installation hold. Then:

GITHUB_BRANCH=REVIEWED_INSTALL_BRANCH bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup-flux.sh

The script requires the exact confirmation BOOTSTRAP and a GitHub token via environment or hidden prompt. Bootstrap changes the cluster and can commit and push to GitHub. It creates a write-enabled SSH deploy key for image automation; the private key is stored in a Kubernetes Secret. Defaults are owner raiken-mf, repository robrowser_docker, branch main, path deploy/clusters/default, and both image controllers. Existing Flux drift or incomplete resources cause an error, not an automatic repair. Never print tokens, kubeconfigs or credential-bearing URLs.

docs.title: Ragnarok GitOps
docs.text: After K3s, storage, Longhorn and Flux are ready, provision the MariaDB operator and follow the fresh stack runbook. Keep the application reconcilers paused until the controlled activation described in GitOps.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Image / service Contents Build tree robrowser Node.js, Vite, pinned roBrowserLegacy frontend images/robrowser remote Apache, PHP 8.4, PHP RemoteClient, ROEnglishRE, client resources images/remote wsproxy WebSocket proxy to internal game services images/wsproxy rathena Login/character/map servers images/rathena hercules Alternative Compose game-server image images/hercules

The Apache image does not clone or contain the frontend. Only the frontend owns index.html.template. /remote/ and the pinned RemoteClient .htaccess remain on the Apache service; / on that service is its static status page.

docs.title: Configuration sources
docs.text:
.env-tmpl is a starting template; preserve/edit the existing local .env. Never commit passwords, private bootstrap output or client assets.

Setting Template value Compose fallback Kubernetes fallback Internal port PORT_FRONTEND 30000 3000 30000 3000 PORT_HTTP 30080 8080 30080 8080 PORT_WSPROXY 30599 5999 30599 5999

Compose uses these variables for host ports; Kubernetes templates use them for NodePorts. Changing them does not change container listeners/target ports. HOST must resolve from the browser; the template uses 127.0.0.1 for local access. The Kubernetes base retains the existing host until the staged Flux migration is complete. Set a reachable hostname or IP for remote clients. Vite accepts this hostname, localhost and IP addresses; cross-origin reads are disabled. Configure the browser-facing hostname explicitly when using DNS. Internal names database and ragnarok-login are not public browser hostnames; wsProxy resolves game-service names inside the cluster/network.

  • Compose: the root .env supplies interpolation; the rAthena stack passes selected variables explicitly. Mounts refer to this checkout's client/ directories.
  • Full bootstrap: k8s-all.sh honors ENV_FILE (default repository .env), CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR (default repository client), K8S_NAMESPACE (default ragnarok) and KUBECONFIG (default /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml). It changes to the repository root internally. Use absolute ENV_FILE/CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR paths when running from another worktree.
  • Offline renderers: k8s-render-web-manifests.sh honors ENV_FILE; render-k8s-bootstrap.py accepts --env-file explicitly. Bootstrap objects inherit K8S_NAMESPACE; an explicit value in the selected environment file takes precedence.
  • Flux: reads deploy/k8s/base/ through deploy/k8s/overlays/flux; it does not read local .env, rerun the renderer or upload local client files. The existing cluster's Flux Kustomization patches its own hostname; configure that patch for your installation before reconciliation.
  • Compatibility entrypoints: k8s-robrowser.sh forwards to full bootstrap, check-only by default. It no longer independently deletes resources or restarts deployments. --apply requires full-stack preflight, not a web-only update. MariaDB accepts ENV_FILE but permits only fresh installation without Flux or existing operator infrastructure.

The web ConfigMap contains HOST, the three ports, SERVER_NAME, SET_PRERENEWAL and PACKETVER. rathena-config contains non-secret DB/game configuration. The private bootstrap Secret supplies both password (operator) and MARIADB_PASSWORD (game containers), plus configured interserver credentials. Passwords never belong in a Git-managed ConfigMap.

docs.title: Image-tag compatibility
docs.text:
VITE_IMAGE_TAG still selects the frontend/robrowser image. Legacy ROBROWSER_IMAGE_TAG remains an Apache/remote fallback; REMOTE_IMAGE_TAG takes precedence for that service. RATHENA_IMAGE_TAG and WSPROXY_IMAGE_TAG remain. Do not silently reinterpret these existing variables during the image rename.

k8s-all.sh defaults to reviewed SHA tags from the Flux overlay and rejects empty or stable selections. The standalone renderer/component scripts can default to stable, so explicitly select reviewed releases before using their output for production. See Image revisions.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Docker Engine/Compose and local client files are prerequisites. From repository root, validate without printing the expanded environment:

docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/compose/docker-compose-common.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose-rathena.yml config --quiet

Starting Compose changes local containers; use it only for the intended local installation, not to update a Kubernetes deployment:

./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh rathena detached
./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh hercules detached

The starter uses the repository-root .env for Compose interpolation; set ENV_FILE to select another file. Shell environment variables take precedence. The first argument selects the emulator; ./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh detached is not valid. Default ./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh runs rAthena in the foreground. ./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh stop stops the Compose stacks; ./scripts/sh/compose/start-compose.sh down removes them. Stopping or removing the stacks does not require database credentials or an env file. Starting either game stack requires nonempty database and interserver passwords; MariaDB also requires a root password for initialization. Hercules starts its character and map servers after the preceding server's TCP healthcheck succeeds. Its database initializer skips a nonempty database; inspect and recover a partially initialized database before retrying. Changing the interserver credentials requires updating the existing database account as well.

The starter checks Docker and Compose but does not install them. The historical ./start.sh entrypoint forwards to it. Compose mounts deploy/compose/conf.d read-only; local configuration files there are ignored by Git. Before restarting an existing Compose installation, copy any operator-owned overrides from the former database/conf.d directory to deploy/compose/conf.d and review them. The old directory remains ignored to protect overrides left behind. Kubernetes explicitly configures utf8mb4_unicode_ci and UTC. Verify collation and time-zone requirements before moving data between the two environments. Compose does not configure persistent database storage; plan and test persistence and backups before using it for valuable data.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
The old unsafe rAthena installer was disabled without replacement because it exposed credentials and interpolated SQL. Its unused exit-only placeholder has been removed; no alternative legacy installation is enabled. For new deployments, use the separately reviewed fresh-install procedure; its preflight is read-only and cluster changes require separate approval.

Cluster setup, fresh stack installation and normal operation are separate procedures. Existing K3s, Longhorn, MariaDB operator and Flux must not be reinstalled as routine updates. Manual MariaDB installation requires explicitly reviewed MARIADB_OPERATOR_VERSION (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for both charts. No latest/default version is selected. Missing prerequisites or webhook endpoints abort. See the separate storage and operator plans.

With Flux CRDs present, full bootstrap requires both expected Kustomizations in flux-system and all listed Kustomizations across namespaces suspended. This conservative gate can block unrelated active tenants: use normal GitOps changes instead of bypassing ownership checks.

Client uploads write unique .upload-* siblings, verify byte counts, flush and rename only after successful streaming. Failed uploads preserve the previous destination and attempt scoped temporary-file cleanup. API loss or process/node termination can prevent cleanup. This is per-file atomicity, not whole-client release atomicity or cryptographic content verification.

To review web manifests without changing the cluster:

ENV_FILE=/absolute/path/to/.env bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-render-web-manifests.sh /tmp/ragnarok-web-review
kubectl kustomize deploy/k8s/overlays/flux

The renderer emits remote.yaml, robrowser.yaml, wsproxy.yaml and robrowser-config.yaml. Review ports, namespace, public HOST, image references and non-secret values before proposing Git changes. It does not automatically replace the concrete manifests or update Flux. Never copy private bootstrap output into deploy/k8s/base/.

docs.title: Translation, mounts and overrides
docs.text:
The remote image includes the pinned ROEnglishRE source. At container startup, SET_PRERENEWAL=1 selects the Pre-Renewal translation layer; 0 selects Renewal. Restart the container after changing runtime settings. The rAthena image also uses SET_PRERENEWAL at build time to select its server ruleset; keep the build and runtime settings consistent. Required source directories are checked, and the ROENGLISH_* runtime options control optional layers.

images/remote/repository_override/ is copied after translations into the Apache document root. Use remote/data and remote/System for translation overrides. images/robrowser/repository_override/ is copied into /app after npm install and the default frontend template. Most local payloads stay ignored by Git and are not present in clean CI builds; the two API-module fix files are intentional versioned exceptions. See the iframe fix.

At startup, remote merges readonly /opt/client_files/data and System into its writable translation tree, preserving the base and giving user loose files precedence. Resources/BGM/AI retain their readonly mounts. Bootstrap uploads local assets into the client-data PVC before starting the web deployments.

docs.title: Existing-checkout override folder rename
docs.text: Git does not move ignored user files. If converting an OLD checkout, preserve the old Apache images/robrowser/repository_override payload under images/remote, and the old images/vite/repository_override frontend payload under images/robrowser. Do not mix the two runtime payloads. This is a manual local-file migration, not a reason to reset a namespace or overwrite working assets.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
• images/robrowser: Node.js/Vite frontend, package/lockfile overlay and client template.
  • images/remote: Apache/PHP, RemoteClient, translations and client-file configuration.
  • images/rathena and images/hercules: game-server images; images/wsproxy: proxy.
  • build/dependencies.env: exact upstream Git revision pins.
  • deploy/compose: local runtime; deploy/k8s/base: concrete GitOps base; deploy/k8s/templates: bootstrap templates; deploy/k8s/overlays: release selection. The base is authoritative for shared resource definitions; CI compares each parameterized bootstrap template with its base using standard values.
  • deploy/clusters/default: Flux parent/source and installation-specific child.
  • scripts/sh, scripts/py and scripts/js: project-wide administration and checks; image-specific tests and helpers, including the wsproxy stdin test, live with their image. The root start.sh remains the Compose entrypoint.
  • docs: installation, operation, development, release and security guidance.

The separate custom-scripts repository owns K3s/Longhorn/Flux bootstrap wrappers; it is not vendored here. Do not change its storage/bootstrap behavior as a side effect of an application or documentation fix.

docs.title: Safe local work
docs.text:
Use a feature branch or separate worktree based on current main. Keep existing .env, client assets and ignored overrides outside any cleanup/reset operation. Never run broad git clean, hard resets or image/volume pruning to make a checkout look tidy. Inspect the worktree's tracked, untracked AND ignored files before removing it; archive any configuration that must survive.

A branch is not proved merged merely because its PR is closed: rebased/squashed history may need further review. Preserve ambiguous refs rather than force-delete them. Remote-branch deletion requires explicit permission.

The full bootstrap can use absolute ENV_FILE and CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR paths from another worktree. Compose's bind paths/env_file remain rooted in its checkout; ENV_FILE is not a general Compose override. See deployment.

docs.title: Build the two web images
docs.text:
These commands build local test images, not Kubernetes deployments or registry releases. Source the versioned dependency pins, not an arbitrary upstream HEAD:

set -a
source build/dependencies.env
set +a
docker build -f images/remote/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg REMOTECLIENT_REPOSITORY="$REMOTECLIENT_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg REMOTECLIENT_REF="$REMOTECLIENT_REF" \
  --build-arg ROENGLISH_REPOSITORY="$ROENGLISH_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg ROENGLISH_REF="$ROENGLISH_REF" -t remote:ci .
docker build -f images/robrowser/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg ROBROWSER_REPOSITORY="$ROBROWSER_REPOSITORY" \
  --build-arg ROBROWSER_REF="$ROBROWSER_REF" -t robrowser:ci .

The remote container selects its translation layer at startup with SET_PRERENEWAL; the rAthena build uses the same setting to select its compiled ruleset. The frontend alone fetches roBrowserLegacy; do not add that source tree to remote. Both web images fetch their pinned sources in separate build stages; Git is not installed in their runtime images. Remote retains the complete ROEnglishRE tree for runtime generation. The frontend retains its full locked npm dependencies because CI runs its tests in the same image. Project-owned npm manifest/lockfile are installed with npm ci. Update the lockfile and source pin together when the new upstream revision needs a dependency change. The locked jsdom 31 test dependency requires Node.js ^22.22.2, ^24.15.0 or >=26. The cursor test normalizes its expected zero translation through the DOM CSS serializer; its position and scene-loop assertions remain unchanged. The rAthena build preserves the upstream or override custom header and applies validated packet-key build arguments after it. The Compose initializer runs the image entrypoint with database initialization enabled before starting the servers.

docs.title: Validation without Kubernetes deployment
docs.text:
Offline/fake-API checks:

python3 scripts/py/check-k8s-bootstrap.py
python3 scripts/py/check-k8s-all.py
bash scripts/sh/ci/check-platform-config.sh
kubectl kustomize deploy/k8s/overlays/flux >/dev/null

The bootstrap tests use synthetic fixtures/fake kubectl, check confidentiality, abort paths and component ordering. They do not install a real stack. Real k8s-all.sh --check contacts the selected cluster read-only and expects paused Flux; it is unsuitable as an active-cluster CI/operations command.

After building the local images, the Docker checks start/remove their own test containers/networks. Do not confuse them with cluster acceptance:

bash images/remote/tests/check-roenglish.sh remote:ci
bash scripts/sh/ci/check-image-boundaries.sh remote:ci robrowser:ci
python3 scripts/py/check-image-overrides.py
python3 images/robrowser/tests/check-api-module.py robrowser:ci
python3 scripts/py/check-compose.py remote:ci robrowser:ci
python3 scripts/py/check-dockerfile-configs.py
bash images/rathena/tests/check-entrypoint.sh

The Dockerfile configuration check requires PyYAML, envsubst and a C compiler. check-compose.py reads this checkout's .env-tmpl by default; COMPOSE_TEST_ENV_FILE selects an explicit alternative. It isolates the web services on temporary networks and loopback ephemeral ports. CLIENT_TEST_ROOT optionally points to readonly client fixtures. On case-insensitive filesystems, the two case-conflict fixtures are skipped; run them on a case-sensitive filesystem for full coverage. check-roenglish.sh builds/tests the additional Pre-Renewal variant. The upstream-layout check clones pinned sources temporarily; it does not modify their original repositories.

The API iframe override is bound to the pinned upstream HTML. The layout gate detects changes needing a rebase. Other local override payloads stay ignored and are not supplied to clean GitHub Actions builds.

docs.title: CI build caches and release boundaries
docs.text:
The required validate job runs on every pull request, including documentation changes; documentation-only PRs skip Docker builds. Image, workflow, deployment and selected integration-helper changes exercise web and proxy smoke tests. Isolated monitor and bootstrap script changes retain configuration checks but skip those smoke builds. See the CI/CD audit for the full inventory. rAthena validation builds only when its inputs or dependency pins change. Hercules is Compose-config validated and included in the AMD64/ARM64 PR image security scan matrix; it is not published by the release workflow. Hercules builds in a separate stage and retains its complete built server tree in the runtime image without the compiler or Git. wsProxy installs its locked dependencies in a build stage; its runtime image contains Node.js but not npm. After building both images, run bash scripts/sh/ci/check-runtime-images.sh hercules:ci wsproxy:ci to check runtime dependencies, permissions and the proxy handshake without a database or external network. The root .dockerignore affects the root-context web images, not wsProxy, whose build context is images/wsproxy; changing it alone does not rebuild wsProxy.

Buildx stores AMD64 test layers in separate GitHub Actions scopes ci-remote-amd64, ci-robrowser-amd64, ci-wsproxy-amd64 and ci-rathena-amd64. Renewal and Pre-Renewal remote builds share the same local Buildx builder in the validation job, as do the isolated override fixtures. GitHub isolates PR caches from main; never store credentials in layers or cache. BuildKit matches Dockerfile commands, base images, build arguments and copied inputs, so affected layers and subsequent layers rebuild when their inputs change. External package repositories are not cache keys: cached test images are not proof that the latest patches were fetched.

Release candidates are built separately on main and scanned on both AMD64 and ARM64. The remote and robrowser release builds deliberately use no-cache to refresh mutable OS packages. wsproxy retains its uncached release build. rAthena imports the AMD64 CI scope and its multi-platform GHCR buildcache and exports only the latter; BuildKit matches platform-specific layers. The scoped CI cache has one writer per workflow/ref, while the release cache has one writer per image and main CI runs are serialized. Publish promotes the exact security-approved candidate digests; it never rebuilds from these caches. The scans, SBOMs, release tags and draft image-pin PR remain mandatory. If stable's source revision differs from the reviewed Flux pin, release recovery rebuilds and rescans the image. This can repeat expensive work while a GitOps PR awaits review. Publishing now reconciles a durable approval journal into one PR with immutable source tags; see publishing protocol. The rebuild cost remains separate from publishing idempotency.

On a cold or evicted cache, BuildKit rebuilds normally; exports use ignore-error=true so an unavailable cache does not skip a test. Inspect the build action's import/export messages and CACHED lines, image scope, branch, platform and changed build arguments when diagnosing misses. GitHub cache eviction, limits and first-run warmup affect hit rates. To diagnose stale cache, compare a fresh no-cache test build and inspect its inputs; do not bypass release scans. BuildKit cache mounts are not exported by the GHA backend by default, so no cross-run npm cache-mount persistence is assumed.

docs.title: Documentation checks
docs.text:
The documentation workflow runs a strict build on relevant pull requests and publishes the site on main changes to docs or mkdocs.yml. A local strict build is the relevant pre-PR check:

python3 -m venv /tmp/robrowser-docs-tools
/tmp/robrowser-docs-tools/bin/pip install mkdocs-material
/tmp/robrowser-docs-tools/bin/mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/robrowser-docs-site

Use a fresh temporary directory if those paths already contain someone else's work. Do not commit generated site files, test output, reports or private bootstrap artifacts. PR CI's required validate check is scope-sensitive: documentation-only changes do not exercise image builds. Record the actual local/CI checks in the PR.

docs.title: Contribution scope
docs.text: Keep changes small, describe behavior and validation, and obtain the appropriate merge/deployment approvals. Current application fixes use their own reviewed PRs; remaining graphics/Lua/GRF-content/gameplay issues are outside documentation cleanup. See validation boundaries and security.

docs.title: Fresh Ragnarok stack on an existing cluster
docs.text: This runbook is for an empty application installation on an already prepared cluster. It is not the maintenance procedure for the running GitOps stack. The example installation has completed: both Flux Kustomizations are active/Ready and browser login succeeded. Nothing here says to suspend that working installation.

docs.title: Prerequisites and approval gate
docs.text:
K3s/node access, Longhorn, a ready MariaDB operator/webhook and its CRDs must already exist. The cluster guide explains the separate infrastructure scripts and their side effects. k8s-all.sh checks these prerequisites; it does not install/upgrade them. Complete K3s and storage first, then Longhorn, then Flux, before the Ragnarok bootstrap. The infrastructure setup scripts do not install the MariaDB operator.

For a genuinely new stack, obtain installation approval, review storage and image pins, and ensure the target namespace is absent. Do not delete a working namespace or reuse this procedure as a backup restore. The verified installation deliberately used a new empty ragnarok database; no old data required recovery.

The manual bootstrap requires both existing Flux Kustomizations paused. The Git state used for activation must hold ragnarok-stack at suspend:true until its release is approved. See controlled activation. The current operational main has suspend:false; it is not an installation hold. Establish a reviewed hold for the target installation before bootstrap, rather than assuming a one-off pause survives parent reconciliation.

docs.title: Local configuration and context
docs.text:
Use a reviewed current checkout without overwriting local .env, client files or ignored override payloads. A separate worktree can use the originals by absolute path. For example, after choosing the intended checkout:

export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.kube/config"
export ENV_FILE="$PWD/.env"
export CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR="$PWD/client"
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes -o wide
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system

These are environment/read-only checks. Never print kubeconfig, .env, Secret data or registry credentials. Use an authorized kubeconfig for the target; copying a file with a localhost server address to another host is not sufficient.

Set HOST to a browser-reachable hostname or IP and choose the appropriate ports. Keep the existing variable names and fallbacks. All database and interserver credentials are read from local .env exactly as configured; bootstrap does not invent passwords or restore backups.

Expected local layout:

client/
  resources/DATA.INI   # case-sensitive, references the available GRFs
  resources/*.grf
  AI/
  BGM/
  data/
  System/

Before installation, verify source files fit the 15Gi client PVC. MariaDB uses new 5Gi Longhorn storage. A previous namespace's Bound PVC status does not establish a recovery path after deletion; this runbook assumes an empty new DB.

docs.title: Read-only bootstrap check
docs.text:
bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-all.sh --check

No argument also defaults to --check. It loads the local configuration, renders private temporary Secrets/ConfigMaps, checks API errors, operator/storage availability, image tag selection, paused Flux, port ownership and DATA.INI/GRF source completeness. It performs no cluster writes and removes its private temporary files. It intentionally rejects active Flux even though this mode is read-only; it is a bootstrap preflight, not a general operations health check.

The web renderer can emit non-secret review files separately, but its standalone image defaults may be stable. The full bootstrap chooses reviewed SHA tags from the Flux overlay unless compatible image-tag overrides were explicitly supplied. Review those overrides; never treat an invented old-name SHA or stable as release provenance. See configuration sources.

docs.title: Full installation — changes the cluster
docs.text:
Only after the installation approval and a successful preflight:

bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-all.sh --apply

The script runs the complete application sequence:

  1. Recheck paused Flux/prerequisites. An existing namespace requires an expressly approved --reconcile retry. API/auth failures abort, not masquerade as NotFound. The script never deletes a namespace or resumes Flux.
  2. Apply the labeled/hardened namespace and restrictive DB network policy, then private mariadb-root-secret/mariadb-user-secret and rathena-config, followed by the .env-derived robrowser-config.
  3. Apply MariaDB, Database, User and Grant CRs and wait for their Ready conditions. The user Secret contains both password (operator) and MARIADB_PASSWORD (rAthena), plus the configured interserver user/password. No password goes in a Git-managed ConfigMap or local command argument.
  4. Create the client PVC/non-root loader, upload CLIENT_SOURCE_DIR folders and check streamed file sizes. Stop on failure before starting the web services.
  5. Start login, char and map in dependency order. Login's INIT_DB=true entrypoint imports the empty schema and Renewal/Pre-Renewal SQL according to SET_PRERENEWAL, then configures the interserver account. Char/map do not initialize the DB. A private in-pod SQL check verifies the account row.
  6. Deploy/wait for wsProxy, remote and robrowser. Check an actual wsProxy WebSocket handshake and parse the mounted first GRF using RemoteClient PHP. List pods/services/PVCs; Flux remains paused for the separate adoption gate.

Secret output is an owner-only temporary file (directory 0700, file 0600), not logged or committed. The offline renderer rejects overwriting an existing output file. A failure aborts; it does not reset data or suppress SQL failures. Diagnose it before approving --apply --reconcile for a partial-install retry.

docs.title: Acceptance and GitOps adoption
docs.text:
Use the read-only operations checks, then test the frontend in a real browser: rendered host/ports, iframe startup, RemoteClient requests/CORS, external WebSocket connection, login and map loading. Keep client content errors distinct from Kubernetes readiness.

For first adoption, activate the parent while the child is explicitly held in Git; verify parent revision/Ready and the child pause, then separately review the Git change enabling the child. See the precise sequence. Git-managed configuration/pins must match the installed .env-derived settings. Secrets and populated client contents remain private/bootstrap managed; do not commit or recreate them to make GitOps adopt the stack.

docs.title: What was actually verified
docs.text: The completed example installation and login were confirmed by the operator on 2026-11-02. The empty MariaDB 11.8.6 schema/bootstrap was also tested in disposable Docker containers against the published rAthena image. CI tests secret rendering, failure/ordering behavior through a fake kubectl, and the frontend/remote images. Those fake-API tests are not substitutes for live acceptance. Commands in this runbook are future procedures and were not re-executed during documentation cleanup.

docs.title: Vite iframe HTML-proxy regression
docs.text: The pinned upstream applications/api/api.js creates a FRAME URL as api.html? + Math.random() + location.hash. On a cold Vite server, requesting that cache-busted page transformed the inline module into api.html?html-proxy&index=0.js. That module request returned HTTP 500: No matching HTML proxy module found. Warming the unqueried HTML first can hide the problem, which is why the old root/API-script HTTP smoke checks missed it.

docs.title: Project-owned override
docs.text:
images/robrowser/repository_override/applications/api/api.html changes only the inline module into <script type="module" src="./api-bootstrap.js"></script>. The neighboring api-bootstrap.js contains the exact extracted upstream logic. Its relative dynamic import still resolves to ../../src/main.js because the external module stays in the same directory as the HTML page.

Parent/opener source filtering, the one-shot configuration listener, ROConfig assignment before the import, the ready reply after successful import and the error handler are preserved. The import map, styles/preloader and HTML remain. The random query, Firefox/hash behavior and upstream api.js are unchanged. No upstream repository, package dependency, source revision, runtime security, port setting or Kubernetes resource is changed.

These two files are intentionally versioned exceptions to the local override ignore rules and keep the override directory in Git without a placeholder. The Compose smoke test checks both API override files rather than an empty marker. Other custom override payloads remain ignored. A source-pin update must recheck this extraction: check-upstream-layout.sh runs check-api-override.py against the actual fetched upstream HTML and rejects a stale override instead of silently masking an upstream bootstrap change.

docs.title: Regression checks
docs.text:
After building the normal pinned frontend image:

python3 images/robrowser/tests/check-api-module.py robrowser:ci

The test starts/removes its own container on an ephemeral loopback host port. It first requests query-bearing iframe HTML without warming the unqueried page, fetches every module URL returned by Vite, and verifies JavaScript/HTTP 200 for several query/hash/no-query variants. It also requests the real transformed /src/main.js entry. The same test fails against the pre-fix image with the original HTTP 500 proxy error.

check-api-handshake.cjs then executes the real api.js and the Vite-served external bootstrap using Node VM modules. It checks random iframe URLs, config polling/ready cleanup, rejected foreign-window messages, parent and opener initialization, one-shot setup, delayed import readiness and import failure. Only engine execution is stubbed here: the real engine URL is independently requested through Vite. This is not a full graphical browser/gameplay test. The regression is required in PR/main CI and needs no added npm dependencies.

docs.title: Verification and current deployment
docs.text:
Local ARM64 tests reproduced the old 500 response and passed after extraction. CI includes the HTTP/module and handshake checks. The fix merged in PR #88; its published ARM64-capable frontend release was selected through PR #89. After the completed Kubernetes/GitOps adoption the operator confirmed successful browser login. Both Flux Kustomizations are now active/Ready; the former paused installation state is no longer an operating instruction.

These tests do not close separate graphics, Lua, GRF-content or gameplay issues. See validation coverage and normal operations.

docs.title: Source of truth and current state
docs.text: deploy/clusters/default/flux-system/gotk-sync.yaml defines the GitRepository and parent Kustomization flux-system. Its desired path is deploy/clusters/default; it manages the child object in ragnarok-app.yaml. Both use the same source. The child path is deploy/k8s/overlays/flux, whose base is deploy/k8s/base. The shared base retains the existing host during migration stage one; the existing cluster's child Kustomization patches robrowser-config with its installation-specific browser hostname. Set that patch to your own reachable hostname or IP before adopting this configuration. For an existing installation, first deploy this stage-one child patch while retaining the old shared HOST, then verify the parent has applied it before a separate change sets the shared HOST to 127.0.0.1. Otherwise the child can reconcile loopback before the parent applies its patch. Roll back by restoring the previous shared HOST before removing the child patch. These are separate reviewed changes, not automatic steps. There is no explicit dependsOn in these manifests; the parent/child management relationship is not an application-health dependency.

docs.title: Cluster path migration
docs.text:
The former paths clusters/pi-cluster and deploy/overlays/flux are absent from the migration commit. An operator must suspend both existing Kustomizations before merging it and keep them suspended until both live paths are patched. Record their inventories, applied revisions and workload health before the merge; compare the rendered resources and live inventories, including namespaces, PVCs and StatefulSets. Both reconcilers prune: stop if identities or ownership differ. Do not rebootstrap Flux. The local setup wrapper defaults to CLUSTER_PATH=deploy/clusters/default and reports existing drift without repair.

After the reviewed migration is merged, set APPROVED_SHA to its exact main commit. The following commands are operator actions on the intended cluster:

: "${APPROVED_SHA:?Set the reviewed migration commit SHA}"
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" path="}{.spec.path}{" suspended="}{.spec.suspend}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl -n flux-system patch kustomization flux-system --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"path":"./deploy/clusters/default","suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n flux-system patch kustomization ragnarok-stack --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"path":"./deploy/k8s/overlays/flux","suspend":true}}'
flux reconcile source git flux-system -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get gitrepository flux-system -o jsonpath='{.status.artifact.revision}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" path="}{.spec.path}{" suspended="}{.spec.suspend}{"\n"}{end}'

Stop unless both paths and suspended=true are correct and the source artifact revision is exactly main@sha1:$APPROVED_SHA. Freeze merges to main until both reconcilers have applied that revision; the GitRepository continues polling while Kustomizations are suspended. The Git child spec is suspend:false: resuming the parent can resume the child immediately, before the parent reports Ready. Both paths, source and inventories must therefore be approved before resuming the parent:

flux resume kustomization flux-system -n flux-system
flux reconcile kustomization flux-system -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack -o yaml

Verify the parent Ready condition and applied revision, and the child path and state. If the child is still suspended, resume it with flux resume kustomization ragnarok-stack -n flux-system. Verify both applied revisions, inventories and workload health using the commands below. Flux Ready does not prove application health (wait: false).

flux get sources git -n flux-system
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack -o yaml
kubectl -n ragnarok get deployments,statefulsets,pods,pvc
kubectl -n ragnarok get mariadb database
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/ragnarok-login
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/ragnarok-char
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/ragnarok-map
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/remote
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/robrowser
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/wsproxy

Record the inventory and applied revision securely without publishing private configuration. For rollback, suspend both reconcilers immediately. Keep them suspended while a reviewed revert restores both former directories and matching pins; merge it and verify the source artifact is exactly the approved revert SHA. Freeze merges to main until rollback completes. Only then patch both old paths while retaining the suspension:

flux suspend kustomization flux-system -n flux-system
flux suspend kustomization ragnarok-stack -n flux-system
# Merge the reviewed revert and verify its source artifact revision first.
flux reconcile source git flux-system -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get gitrepository flux-system -o jsonpath='{.status.artifact.revision}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n flux-system patch kustomization flux-system --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"path":"./clusters/pi-cluster","suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n flux-system patch kustomization ragnarok-stack --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"path":"./deploy/overlays/flux","suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" path="}{.spec.path}{" suspended="}{.spec.suspend}{"\n"}{end}'

Stop unless the artifact is the approved revert revision, both old paths and suspensions are correct, and the source and inventories are approved. Then resume the parent:

flux resume kustomization flux-system -n flux-system
flux reconcile kustomization flux-system -n flux-system

The parent may resume the child immediately here too. Verify both paths, source, inventories and health after resuming; resume the child separately only if it remains suspended. If the revert is unavailable, leave both suspended and the existing workloads running. Never delete or recreate Flux objects, workloads, PVCs or PVs. A fresh install requires the suspended-child procedure below. The later shared-HOST migration remains a separate change after the child patch is confirmed; this path migration does not activate it.

The last operator-verified operating state had both reconcilers active/Ready. The child Git spec is suspend:false. An absent suspend field on the parent also means active. The last operator-confirmed installation revision was 109430d1 (2026-11-02); later documentation-only merges can advance source/applied revisions without changing workload specifications.

Local .env is not read by Flux. Review and commit non-secret ConfigMaps, selectors, ports and release pins explicitly. Private bootstrap supplies Secrets and client PVC contents. wait:false on the application means Flux Ready proves reconciliation, not healthy DB/game/frontend processes.

docs.title: Controlled first activation
docs.text:
This section is for a new installation, not normal operation. It describes the hold used during installation; it is not a request to reapply it to today's working stack.

  1. Have a reviewed Git installation state explicitly holding the child at suspend:true. During manual bootstrap both existing reconcilers stay paused. The full application installer refuses an active reconciler and never resumes it. The GitRepository manifest in that installation state must also reference the intended repository and installation branch, not the checked-in main branch. Verify the rendered source and live source revision before resuming the parent; otherwise the parent can switch sources and remove the installation hold.
  2. After bootstrap/acceptance and activation approval, confirm the intended source revision and SSH Secret. Resume only the parent while the Git child hold remains true; wait for the parent's Ready condition and exact applied revision. Verify the child remains suspended. Do not infer application health from this.
  3. Review a separate Git change lifting the child hold (suspend:false). With the parent active, merging it lets the parent update the child and start its reconciliation. A one-off CLI child resume while Git still says true is not durable: the parent would restore the hold.
  4. Verify both Flux revisions/conditions, then actual pods, PVCs, endpoints, frontend, RemoteClient, WebSocket and browser login. Resolve manifest drift from any .env-based manual bootstrap before accepting GitOps ownership.

The completed installation used the reviewed child activation in PR #90. Do not repeat bootstrap or pause/resume working reconcilers for a routine image update.

docs.title: Normal approved-release path
docs.text:
1. Source/dependency changes pass required PR validation and enter main through human review and the repository's branch protection.
  2. Main CI validates the affected images. Container Security builds changed candidates for AMD64/ARM64, applies the existing HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability gate and emits platform SBOMs/approved digest records.
  3. Publish promotes the exact scanned digests, checks their source revision against main ancestry and records approval before promotion. It sets sha-source and stable tags; unchanged components retain their previous releases. Main may advance during scanning; newer approved component releases are never downgraded.
  4. Publish opens a draft GitOps image-bump PR, without enabling auto-merge, updating only the corresponding overlay image tags.
  5. Approve any GitHub Actions runs awaiting approval on the bot-created PR, then review the actual registry digest/source/platforms, CI, component pairing and release approval, then merge that image-pin PR. Active Flux automatically applies the new Git desired state; a manual reconcile command is not required.

This is automatic adoption after approval, not automatic approval of all published images. Publishing stable alone does not change SHA-pinned pods. Review any externally configured auto-merge separately; it is not promised by these workflows. See upstream updates for source-PR and Dependabot review requirements.

docs.title: Normal inspection and optional reconciliation
docs.text:
Read-only:

flux get sources git -n flux-system
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system
kubectl -n flux-system get kustomizations flux-system ragnarok-stack

If an operator explicitly needs to accelerate an approved desired-state change, these are mutating reconciliation requests, not passive health checks:

flux reconcile source git flux-system -n flux-system
flux reconcile kustomization flux-system -n flux-system --with-source
flux reconcile kustomization ragnarok-stack -n flux-system --with-source

Do not run them, resume/suspend Flux or bootstrap the cluster during unrelated documentation/cleanup work. Normal polling already reconciles Git automatically.

docs.title: Recovering from a bad release
docs.text:
Prefer a reviewed Git revert to the last verified component tag/digest, preserving other image pins and configuration. Once merged, verify Flux and application health. Do not substitute newest main into every component tag or roll stable back blindly.

An imperative deployment-only rollback is an emergency action needing explicit approval and coordination with active Flux; otherwise it will reconcile back to Git. Record the previous reference, actual container name and scope. Never use namespace/PVC deletion as rollback, and never restore DB storage without a separate verified recovery plan. See operations.

docs.title: Image references and provenance
docs.text: The authoritative desired selection is deploy/k8s/overlays/flux/kustomization.yaml, not whichever local test image or stable tag happens to exist.

docs.title: Verified installation selection
docs.text:
The following source tags were selected at the confirmed 109430d1 operating baseline (2026-11-02). This table is a dated reference; future approved image PRs can update the overlay independently per component.

Image Role Selected source tag robrowser Node.js/Vite frontend, including the iframe module fix sha-d32fa0e2a793eac80274fcc8d1206a871f4a1376 remote Apache/PHP/RemoteClient/ROEnglishRE sha-6c00eb847d9f65c9b0f4c941140b790177c37470 rathena Login/char/map servers sha-a9c11e46784f25a75cd85cb91cc7fe97e41533f9 wsproxy Game WebSocket proxy sha-ddc424509d376dc1e77f4b6925f3df37fc4caf27

The final-name releases support AMD64 and ARM64. The frontend d32fa0e release passed main CI/security/SBOM/promotion in run 41448256973. The initial final-name web release passed run 41435931124. Those are evidence for those releases, not a claim that later unchanged images were rescanned on every documentation/image-pin commit.

docs.title: Source SHA versus registry digest
docs.text:
• build/dependencies.env pins upstream source repositories. Their commit hashes are not infrastructure release tags.
  • sha-infrastructure-commit tags identify the source build revision for each released image. Components can legitimately have different tags when their build inputs did not change.
  • The OCI org.opencontainers.image.revision annotation records the build source.
  • sha256:… is the exact registry manifest/index digest. A SHA-named tag is still a tag; verify its digest/platform/provenance rather than treating its spelling as cryptographic immutability. stable is explicitly mutable.
  • Newest main can be a documentation/manifest-only commit with no image release. Do not substitute main HEAD into all tags or compare SHA strings alphabetically.

With Docker/buildx available, inspect the actual selected registry reference; this does not deploy it:

docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/raiken-mf/robrowser:sha-d32fa0e2a793eac80274fcc8d1206a871f4a1376

Check the exact digest, source annotation, both architectures and corresponding successful security/promotion artifacts. Runtime inspection should match the intended role: frontend has Node/Vite, remote has Apache/PHP and client files.

docs.title: Publishing protocol
docs.text:
Main validation and all four release-security jobs must succeed before the reusable publisher runs. promote-main permits one registry writer; CI and publishing use GitHub's queue: max (at most 100 pending runs). Queue admission and runner start order are not release chronology: component source commits are ordered by Git ancestry, never by SHA spelling or run number. Overflowed/canceled runs require a rerun; no guarantee extends to unjournaled work that never reached publishing. Executable publisher code is checked out at the validated initiating github.sha, not moving main. Current main pins are read only as reconciliation data. An unadopted release alone no longer forces a rebuild: unchanged components use the verified journal/proof recovery path. Invalid/missing prior revisions and actual component changes still require builds and existing security gates.

The publisher verifies each three-line ready record against this run's candidate digest and OCI source annotation. Before any registry write it records approvals on automation/image-release-state, in image-releases.json. This state branch is not a deployment branch and must never be merged into main or tracked by Flux. The journal retains source, digest, run and attempt for each image/source pair. Restrict its writers to the trusted publishing identity and repository maintainers; it is a security boundary, not an input for arbitrary contributors. Existing Contents/Pull requests/Packages write and Actions read permissions are unchanged.

Publication promotes exact approved digests without rebuilding. Existing sha-* tags are verified, never overwritten; the first journaled digest for a given image/source remains authoritative even if a rerun builds a different digest. stable advances only along main ancestry and never backwards. Source histories that diverge or registry tags that disagree with the journal fail closed.

One gitops/image-bump draft accumulates independent component releases. An existing single bot-owned legacy image-bump PR is reused instead. The Contents API updates only the Flux overlay using its blob SHA; conflicts trigger bounded re-read/reconciliation, preserving other PR files and newer pins. Main pins that advanced while a PR was pending are carried forward, not reverted. No force push, automatic merge, branch-protection change or alternate token is used. Multiple already-open legacy PRs require a one-time human consolidation before rollout; the publisher refuses to choose or close them automatically.

Interrupted registry or PR updates are recovered from the journal on a subsequent successful invocation, including one with no new ready records. Published legacy stable/open-PR tags absent from the journal require a retained ready artifact from a main CI run whose four security jobs succeeded, plus matching registry digest/source. Missing/expired proof requires human investigation or a fresh gated release, not a bypass. Journal updates must succeed before new publication. There is no background retry daemon; rerun the failed CI publishing job or allow the next successful main release. Preserve the state branch and approved digests.

docs.title: GitHub prerequisites and limitations
docs.text:
• Repository settings must permit GITHUB_TOKEN to create/update PRs and write the two automation branches; rulesets restricting these writes can fail closed.
  • GitHub currently puts GITHUB_TOKEN-created/updated PR workflows in an approval-required state. A user with write access selects Approve workflows to run for the current head. Required checks and human approval still gate merge; approve again after later updates where required. No additional secret or automated approval bypass is configured.
  • Configure branch protection to require checks on the current head/up-to-date base and dismiss stale approvals as appropriate. These external settings have not been inspected or modified. Do not merge using an earlier head's checks.
  • All automated registry writers must share promote-main. External writers, deletion of protected journal/tag state, manual force-pushes or main-history rewrites are outside the lock guarantee and require operator reconciliation.
  • A PR can merge while publishing runs; main is reread before pin updates, but GitHub merge checks remain the final concurrency boundary. The API/registry protocol, permissions, queue syntax, approval banners, artifact retention and exact digest preservation require real Actions acceptance testing.
  • Old automation branches may retain outdated non-image content or need a base update. The publisher intentionally does not reset/rebase human PR work; resolve merge conflicts through normal review before merging.

Local regressions exercise the current Python publisher only; the retired shell workflow emulator is no longer maintained. Missing publisher code fails the check. Local regression command: python3 scripts/py/check-publishing.py; it is also called by the existing CI/Dockerfile contract checker. Twenty isolated cases cover the six requested scenarios plus CAS, legacy proof, digest mismatch, same-source rebuilds, new main pins and permission failures. Scheduling is modeled under the declared single-writer lock; this is not a live concurrency certification.

References: GitHub concurrency and token-triggered workflows.

docs.title: Adoption and rollback
docs.text:
The generated draft GitOps PR accumulates security-approved pending component tags. With active Flux, merging the approved pin change deploys it automatically; publishing a registry tag does not update an already SHA-pinned Deployment. Do not infer automatic merge approval from installed Flux image controllers.

Record the prior component reference before a rollout. Roll back to its verified tag/digest through a narrow Git change, retaining the other image pins. Follow operations for explicitly approved emergency imperative changes. No old pre-rename Apache image should be mistaken for today's frontend robrowser image.

docs.title: Client resources with the unmodified PHP RemoteClient
docs.text:
The RemoteClient is pinned to the PHP fork's revert merge; its source tree is identical to the pre-custom-resolver revision. CLIENT_RESPATH and CLIENT_DATAINI select the directory containing DATA.INI and GRFs; the existing resources mount supplies them. Its original PHP fallback accepts data/ and BGM/ requests and searches the local data tree and GRFs. It does not provide SYSTEM_PATH, SYSTEMEN_PATH, AI_PATH, DATA_OVERRIDE_PATH, or a System to SystemEN alias.

The image retains the pinned ROEnglishRE source and generates a runtime tree from PACKETVER, SET_PRERENEWAL and the ROENGLISH_* options. Apache serves the selected SystemEN/ and data/ files. The existing roBrowser customItemInfo option selects SystemEN/itemInfo.lua, which loads its original nested SystemEN files. System/ is a separate symlink to the read-only client-data mount, so real original System files remain accessible. Missing SystemEN/, System/ and AI/ files are not resolved from GRFs by the PHP fallback. One Apache redirect maps a missing AI/Util.lua request to the existing data/ai/util.lua GRF path; a loose AI/Util.lua takes priority. The redirect has a relative location and includes the existing CORS policy. The frontend proxies /remote/ to the RemoteClient so browser requests and the redirect remain on the frontend origin in Compose and Kubernetes. An internal rewrite alone cannot replace the redirect: the upstream PHP 404 handler reads the original request URI, so it searches for AI/Util.lua instead of the GRF's data/ai/util.lua. The image also installs ROEnglishRE's PetEvolution.lub once in SystemEN/. Apache serves it for a missing System/PetEvolutionCln.lub; a loose original takes priority. Similar targeted fallbacks serve CheckAttendance and PrivateAirplane when their loose System files are absent. At startup the image snapshots these four specific regular System files for case-insensitive fallback matching; files with the exact requested spelling use the same snapshot for consistent contents. An existing exact path remains accessible from the mount if no regular-file snapshot exists. Snapshots are refreshed on initialization, and ambiguous case variants fail initialization explicitly. Existing AI and BGM mounts are exposed by the image's existing symlinks. At startup, regular loose files in the readonly client mount's data/ and SystemEN/ are overlaid on the generated tree, without modifying the mount. Matching ASCII names are overlaid without regard to letter case, retaining the generated path spelling. Ambiguous names differing only in ASCII letter case within one source or destination directory fail initialization explicitly. The generator also consolidates ASCII-case variants of directory names from different upstream layers, so their files remain available in one directory; non-ASCII filename bytes are left unchanged. The browser may itself resolve a file from its local GRF before requesting the RemoteClient, so server-side overlays cannot override every browser-local file. The exact pinned upstream generator rules, known script discrepancies and addon inventory are recorded in the upstream inventory.

The pinned client's TownInfo callback returns no success value and replaces each map's entries. The supplied English Towninfo stops after its first callback; serving it at a different path does not fix that client incompatibility. The client already falls back from the missing System quest aliases to SystemEN/OngoingQuests.lub; its Lua 5.1 execution creates 11,363 entries.

The optional System/Font/SCDream4.otf, data/msgstringtable.csv, System/OngoingQuestInfoList.lub, System/Towninfo.lub, AI/AI_M.lua and data/luafiles514/lua files/hateffectinfo/hateffectids.lub depend on the operator's client data. They are not supplied as placeholders. Availability and warnings vary with the mounted loose files and GRFs.

The image retains upstream request handling and applies standard Apache access controls to protect GRFs, configuration, application PHP files and internal directories from direct HTTP access.

docs.title: Existing GitOps cluster: operation and recovery
Compose database persistence plan
docs.text:
This is a proposed migration, not an executed change. Shared Compose currently does not declare /var/lib/mysql persistence; an existing container may own an anonymous image volume. Never attach a fresh empty volume as an automatic upgrade.

  1. With explicit target approval, record the actual database volume, engine/image version, ownership and free space without exposing credentials.
  2. Create a private consistent backup and prove restoration into an isolated database. Retain the original volume and test rollback before migration.
  3. Stop writers in an approved maintenance window and take a final backup. For existing installations, prepare an installation-only external-volume override pointing to the verified original volume. Do not commit host-specific identity.
  4. For fresh installations, propose a named /var/lib/mysql volume only after testing both emulator stacks, initialization and persistence across recreation.
  5. Verify accounts, schema and game login before resuming writes. Retain original data until human acceptance. Never use volume pruning/deletion in this plan.

docs.title: MariaDB operator upgrade plan
docs.text:
The fresh-only installer requires MARIADB_OPERATOR_VERSION for both charts and refuses existing Flux/operator infrastructure before Helm writes. No chart version has been certified here and no installed release was inspected.

  1. With permission, record installed chart/CRD, Kubernetes and application versions, Flux ownership and database/PVC state. Verify authoritative compatibility and release notes for the exact proposed pair; equal versions alone prove nothing.
  2. Test backup restoration and operator/CRD transitions in an isolated environment matching relevant architectures/schema. Review conversion, webhooks and storage immutability. Define forward recovery where CRD downgrades are unsafe; Helm rollback is not database restoration.
  3. Propose exact verified versions through the owning GitOps manifests and human review. Do not run fresh installers or create competing Helm ownership live.
  4. Obtain explicit maintenance/target approval, adopt the reviewed Git change and verify operator/webhook, database readiness, unchanged PVC identity and login. PVC/data migration requires separate approval; retain backups until acceptance.

In the verified example installation, both Flux Kustomizations were active/Ready and seven application pods were confirmed Running/ready with successful browser login on 2026-11-02. Do not use installation or bootstrap modes, k8s-all.sh --apply, namespace resets or blanket image/volume pruning for routine maintenance.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Select the intended authorized kubeconfig/context before any action. The application scripts default to /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml; an operator can instead explicitly use an authorized user kubeconfig:

export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/.kube/config"
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes -o wide
flux get sources git -n flux-system
flux get kustomizations -n flux-system
bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup-flux.sh --check
bash scripts/sh/k8s/k8s-setup-storage.sh --check
kubectl -n ragnarok get deployments,statefulsets,pods
kubectl -n ragnarok get pvc,services,endpointslices
kubectl -n ragnarok get events --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl -n longhorn-system get pods
kubectl get storageclass

These commands inspect state; they do not reconcile/install/restart resources. Expected application roles: database-0 (operator StatefulSet), rAthena login/char/map, remote, robrowser and wsProxy. There are six application Deployments plus MariaDB; the confirmed one-replica baseline has seven pods, each 1/1. Names/counts can change with a deliberate reviewed scaling/version change.

Check Ready/available replicas, Bound PVCs, populated EndpointSlices, current Flux source/applied revision and no repeated scheduling/pull/crash errors. Longhorn controller readiness and an existing StorageClass alone do not prove volume health or data recovery; inspect actual relevant volumes when investigating a storage incident, without deleting them.

Read-only workload details, scoped to the actual failing service:

kubectl -n ragnarok describe deployment robrowser
kubectl -n ragnarok logs deployment/robrowser --tail=100
kubectl -n ragnarok logs deployment/remote --tail=100
