kubectl -n ragnarok get deployments -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.template.spec.containers[*].image

Do not dump Secret data, full environments, kubeconfigs or remote URLs with embedded credentials. Sanitize console/network diagnostics, including tokens in Vite/HMR WebSocket query strings, before sharing reports.

docs.title: HTTP, module and game checks
docs.text:
Set these values to the browser-reachable host and ports of your installation, not internal cluster DNS names:

HOST=127.0.0.1
PORT_HTTP=30080
PORT_FRONTEND=30000
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_HTTP/" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_HTTP/remote/System/add-system-folder-files-here.txt" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_FRONTEND/" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_FRONTEND/applications/api/api.js" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_FRONTEND/applications/api/api.html?0.138571" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_FRONTEND/applications/api/api-bootstrap.js" >/dev/null
curl -fsS "http://$HOST:$PORT_FRONTEND/src/Renderer/GR2/GR2ModelRenderer.js" >/dev/null

A successful HTML request is not proof that all browser modules work. Inspect the iframe's module requests and JavaScript console. The API iframe fix in PR #88 externalizes the inline module; its regression checks cover the cache-busted HTML path that previously failed with HTTP 500.

A scoped WebSocket test can be run with operator permission:

kubectl -n ragnarok exec -i deployment/wsproxy -- node - < images/wsproxy/tests/check-wsproxy.cjs

It checks a real handshake, not a game login. A new browser session should verify iframe readiness, public HOST/ports, RemoteClient/CORS and actual login/map loading. The operator confirmed login on the completed installation; continuing graphics, Lua, GRF-content or client issues are separate investigations.

docs.title: RemoteClient quick-health caveat
docs.text: The pinned RemoteClient defaults to lazy GRF indexes. Its quick health endpoint can report 503/grfsLoaded=0 before indexes are loaded, even when the mount is readable and an explicit parser/resource request succeeds. Distinguish this known metric limitation from missing DATA.INI, wrong file case, absent GRFs, permissions, real parse failures or HTTP rewrite errors. Do not enable a large index/cache solely to turn the quick metric green.

docs.title: Normal changes
docs.text:
Use approved release/image-pin PRs. Changing a local .env does not update GitOps-managed ConfigMaps. Review the non-secret rendered Git changes; existing pods need a controlled replacement to consume changed environment values. Credentials remain private; a password change may require coordinated DB/operator/game-account updates, not merely a file edit.

k8s-all.sh --check is deliberately not the active-cluster health command: it requires paused Flux for a manual-bootstrap preflight. Neither --apply nor --reconcile is the ordinary update path.

docs.title: Rollback and failure handling
docs.text:
On failure, collect scoped status/events/logs and identify the failed layer before retrying. Do not rerun installers blindly, bootstrap Flux again, format storage, reset namespaces or delete PVC/PV/Longhorn volumes.

For an image regression, inspect Git history for the last verified component pin and propose a narrow revert. Keep the other component pins unchanged, rerun required checks, then adopt through normal approved GitOps reconciliation. Tag names identify infrastructure source commits, not chronological ordering; verify the registry digest and architecture. Stable is mutable and is not a rollback record.

Emergency imperative example (requires explicit target-only approval and Flux coordination; not executed during cleanup):

kubectl -n ragnarok get deployment robrowser -o jsonpath='{range .spec.template.spec.containers[*]}{.name}{" "}{.image}{"\n"}{end}'
# Record OLD_IMAGE and the actual CONTAINER before changing anything.
kubectl -n ragnarok set image deployment/robrowser "$CONTAINER=$OLD_IMAGE"
kubectl -n ragnarok rollout status deployment/robrowser --timeout=180s

An active reconciler restores its Git desired state; make the approved rollback consistent with Git rather than leaving uncontrolled drift. Do not touch MariaDB, other deployments, configuration or storage for a frontend-only incident.

Storage/DB recovery is a separate operation with a verified backup, scope, credentials and maintenance approval. The fresh-install runbook's automatic empty-DB import is not a restore procedure.

docs.title: Implementation follow-up
docs.text:
The original findings below describe the audit snapshot, not current status. No additional general audit was performed during implementation.

  • F01: temporary sibling uploads, size checks, sync and atomic rename; failed streams preserve old files. Cleanup depends on API availability.
  • F02: inherited namespace preserved; explicit environment-file value wins.
  • F03: executable publisher checkout pinned to validated initiating commit.
  • F10: unchanged unadopted releases recover without rebuilding; invalid revisions and changed component inputs still require security-gated builds.
  • F06/F07: expected suspended Flux owners required, active Kustomizations rejected; old web entrypoint delegates to check-only full bootstrap.
  • F05/F11: fresh MariaDB requires explicit chart version, rejects existing Flux/ operator, checks prerequisites and aborts webhook timeout. Compatible chart release and live upgrade remain uncertified.
  • Requested renderer/standards renames completed with callers updated. Unused disabled rAthena placeholder removed; Compose start wrapper retained.
  • F04: concrete persistence plan only; existing data/volumes untouched. Operator upgrade plan likewise requires approval and restore testing.
  • F08/F09/F12/F13/F14 remain open. No unrelated runtime/resource/translation edits or new dependencies were introduced. Deployment/operations describe limits.

docs.title: Implementation verification
docs.text:
• Tested on macOS with the existing Python 3.15 environment: publisher (20 cases), Dockerfile/configuration contracts, bootstrap/namespace/secret/installer mocks, upload success/interruption/newline filenames, Flux guards, script layout, Compose contract, XERJ monitor, K3s/Flux setup mocks, shell syntax, strict MkDocs and whitespace checks. Dockerfile contracts do not build images.
  • Initial regression failures were expected and became green after fixes. Initial PATH failures for gettext/Docker were resolved using installed tools; no dependencies were installed.
  • Not tested: real Kubernetes/Kustomize/platform rendering (kubectl unavailable), live Actions/registry promotion, AMD64/ARM64 image builds, operator compatibility, data migration/restoration or game login. Network upstream checks and known unsafe override-build tests were not rerun. No live cluster/private client access.
  • Failed gate: platform-config check stops because kubectl is unavailable. Generated documentation remains in owned temporary directories, not the repo.

docs.title: Scope and evidence
docs.text:
This audit covers the working tree based on commit ee80c52835e137bad1e672161ff37452260da1d4, including the publishing changes already present before the audit. The cleanup branch is audit/repository-cleanup-20261110. Existing changes were preserved; no commit, push, pull request, production action or workstation dependency installation was performed. Findings describe this working tree, not necessarily the committed main branch. This is a static audit with selected local regression checks, not production certification.

Before adding this report, the deduplicated Git inventory contained 147 existing public project files: 144 tracked and 3 untracked. One tracked but deleted empty frontend marker is excluded from that count. This report adds one untracked file, bringing the existing public inventory to 148. Directory counts before this report: root 11, .github 10, .vscode 1, build 1, client 5, deploy 31, docs 18, images 42, scripts 28. The inventory below records each path and its role; a role is not a claim that every optional external use was demonstrated.

All project-owned scripts, Dockerfiles, workflow definitions, deployment configuration and public documentation were reviewed across bounded read-only reviews and direct checks. Exceptions to full text inspection:

  • The generated Flux components manifest was inspected for structure, images and RBAC, not every generated CRD field (7,390 lines).
  • npm lockfiles were parsed structurally: lockfile version 3, 471 frontend and 6 proxy package records including their roots. Registry and integrity metadata were inspected; transitive dependency implementations were not audited.
  • The GPLv3 license was identified from its metadata, not analyzed legally.
  • No private configuration or credential contents were inspected.
  • Case-insensitive audio/archive exclusions: 185 MP3 and 3 GRF files. No contents were examined or changed. MP3 names are 01-31, 33-172, 174-186 and 997 under the client BGM directory; the GRFs are CR2, data and rdata under client resources.
  • Other ignored project files: four Finder metadata files and the 40-byte client resource selection INI, inspected only for metadata and public callers. The INI contents were not opened. The ignored inventory also contains 18,507 virtual-environment files and 13 generated Python cache files, excluded. Git internals were not traversed.

docs.title: Architecture judgment
docs.text:
The ownership split is sound: each of the five images owns its runtime and image-specific tests; shared validation/rendering lives under language-specific scripts; Compose, Kubernetes templates, Kustomize bases and Flux installation configuration have distinct homes. Hercules is a supported Compose alternative, not an abandoned duplicate of rAthena. RemoteClient and the Vite frontend are separate services with distinct mounts, build inputs and runtime contracts.

The main complexity is deployment ownership: manual Kubernetes installers, offline rendering and Flux reconciliation coexist. Removing one merely because there is another installer would break operational contracts. Instead, establish one guarded bootstrap owner and make manual entry points enforce that boundary. Base/template duplication supports both fixed GitOps and configurable bootstrap; retain it until generation and parity tests can replace it without identity drift.

The existing unpublished publisher improves release durability with approved digest records, ancestry ordering, a persistent approval journal, compare-and-swap Git updates and one consolidated draft proposal. Its supported recovery states justify the journal and legacy-release recovery tests. They do not justify the retired shell-workflow test emulator, which was removed.

docs.title: Prioritized findings
docs.text:
No P0 was demonstrated. Priorities indicate consequences, not confirmed live incidents. Runtime and external repository settings remain unverified.

Source links use GitHub main for published documentation compatibility. Line references describe the audited local working tree and may differ from main, especially for unpublished publishing changes; the inventory identifies local paths. Remote link availability was not verified.

ID Priority Evidence and consequence Recommendation F01 P1 Client uploader streams directly into the final PVC pathname with tee; the size check runs afterwards. A failed retry can truncate a previously valid asset. Stream into a unique sibling temporary file, verify length or digest, then rename atomically; test interrupted overwrite against an existing fixture. Do not test on private assets. F02 P1 Bootstrap renderer reconstructs the subprocess environment from PATH and defaults, while bootstrap owner inherits K8S_NAMESPACE. A namespace supplied only through the environment can place Secrets/ConfigMap in ragnarok and workloads elsewhere. Resolve one validated settings snapshot for all renderers; test environment-only namespace and precedence. F03 P1 Publish checkout selects moving main, then runs repository publisher code with a write token. A queued approved run can execute publisher code newer than its own validated revision. Check out the initiating SHA for executable code; fetch current main separately for ancestry and CAS. Retain the approval journal and exact scanned digests. This finding is in the pre-existing unpublished workflow changes. F04 P1 Compose database mounts configuration but does not declare /var/lib/mysql. Persistence relies on the image's anonymous-volume behavior; recreation can detach the old data from the replacement container. Add an explicitly managed persistent volume only with a reviewed migration/backup procedure. Do not migrate or delete existing anonymous volumes automatically. F05 P1 MariaDB installation uses unversioned helm upgrade --install for operator and CRDs. Repeating an installation can introduce an unreviewed operator/schema change. Pin a reviewed compatible chart pair and separate installation from approved upgrade. F06 P2 Flux bootstrap guard iterates only returned resources from two named lookups with --ignore-not-found; an empty list passes. Other matching reconcilers are not checked. Require the intended resources when Flux is present and verify all owners of the application resources are suspended before writes. Add absent-resource and extra-owner fixtures. F07 P2 Standalone web installer deletes ingress/configuration and restarts workloads without the guarded bootstrap/Flux protocol. No repository caller was established, but external use is plausible. Retain until the external contract is resolved; then delegate to the guarded owner or formally deprecate with a fail-closed migration path. F08 P2 rAthena workloads and their template lack application readiness/liveness probes and resource requests/limits. Successful rollout alone does not demonstrate an accepting game server. Add measured resource settings and appropriate readiness checks; avoid restart probes that interfere with DB initialization. Keep template/base parity. F09 P2 Override test copies the full local images tree, including ignored override payloads, into its build context; fixed image tags remain afterwards. Build an allowlisted public fixture, use unique tags and provide clearly scoped cleanup. Do not transmit local override data or prune user images. F10 P2 Security scope marks an image changed whenever stable differs from the adopted GitOps pin before comparing inputs. A pending human approval can trigger repeated unrelated rebuilds. Separate release recovery from input-change detection using the existing journal. Keep both-platform vulnerability gates; prove that recovered digests cannot bypass approval. F11 P2 MariaDB installer continues after the webhook endpoint loop exhausts; the later network-policy apply requires envsubst despite an earlier fallback. Failures can occur after partial cluster mutation. Check all prerequisites before writes and fail explicitly on webhook timeout; either require envsubst or provide one complete renderer. F12 P2 Frontend HTML template receives shell substitution into JavaScript without context-specific encoding. Operator-controlled malformed settings can break or inject script. No remote attacker control was established. Validate numeric/date settings and serialize string configuration as JSON instead of raw substitution. F13 P3 Security policy describes password command arguments, while current rAthena DB invocation uses MYSQL_PWD; Apache configuration enables OS tokens/signatures. Correct the credential boundary description; reduce server identification independently. MYSQL_PWD still exposes credentials through process environment to sufficiently privileged readers. F14 P3 Kubernetes MariaDB/BusyBox tags and documentation tooling are not uniformly digest/version pinned or covered by update automation. Add reviewed pin/update ownership rather than treating current scanners as a complete dependency inventory.

Further limited-scope observations: default Kubernetes NodePort validation accepts 1-65535 but does not preflight the cluster's configured service range; storage diagnostics suppress some journal errors and assume an mmcblk0 boot-device naming pattern; historical English-project documentation contains German passages; four public resource/audit pages are not included in the MkDocs navigation. These are follow-up candidates, not evidence of unused functionality.

docs.text:
Tested: macOS, local Python 3.15.2 environment, Bash 3.2 and local Docker. check-script-layout.py passed; check-publishing.py passed all 19 tests; check-k8s-setup.sh passed isolated mocked K3s/Flux cases including server-join rejection; strict MkDocs build passed using the existing environment and a temporary output directory; editor diagnostics found no errors in touched scripts; git diff --check passed. The override test was mistakenly treated as a lightweight check before its side effects were inspected. It built local remote-override-test:remote and remote-override-test:robrowser images and ephemeral containers. The containers were removed by the test; image tags and build cache remain. Build-time npm installation occurred inside the fixture image, not the workstation environment. No production cluster or private asset content was intentionally tested.

Not tested: full Compose smoke after its changed payload assertion, all-image builds, live registry/GitHub workflows and settings, both Linux architectures, hardware/storage behavior, browser/gameplay, deployment/migration, excluded assets and every generated Flux CRD field. Local passing checks do not certify these requirements. MkDocs reports four existing pages outside navigation.

Failed: initial rg lookup (tool unavailable), initial PATH MkDocs lookup (executable available only in the existing virtual environment), and some read-only agent/helper queries; compatible replacements completed. docs.title: AdditionsGenerator: Bestandsaufnahme
docs.text: Stand: ROEnglishRE 680a2f2126c8eb5872bf06cf441685c408ed1358. Grundlage: Upstream-Inventar, der AdditionsGenerator und der Additions-Quellbaum der gepinnten GitHub-Revision sowie read-only roBrowserLegacy/src/DB/DBManager.js. Diese Bestandsaufnahme beruht auf statischer Prüfung; Generator, Tests und Client wurden für sie nicht ausgeführt.

docs.title: Leseschlüssel
docs.text:
D bezeichnet Quelle Additions/data und Ziel Tools/Client/data, S Quelle Additions/SystemEN und Ziel Tools/Client/SystemEN. Relative Pfade gelten auf beiden Seiten; ein Pfeil zeigt eine Umbenennung. Verzeichnisse und Wildcards stehen wie im Batch. texture/<legacy>/map ersetzt den nicht-ASCII-Pfadbestandteil; dessen Byte-Kodierung ist ungeprüft. Menü 0 und Exit kopieren nichts. Datumsausdrücke nennen die im Zweig vorkommenden Vergleiche; sie gelten jeweils nur für die im Batch bedingten Dateien. Bei Gesamtpaketen sind die Anweisungen dateispezifisch, nicht zwangsläufig die Vereinigung der Einzelzweige.

Status aller Zeilen: Auswahl statisch erfasst; tatsächliches Kopierergebnis, Abhängigkeiten, Format und Client-Kompatibilität ungeprüft, soweit unten nicht ausdrücklich belegt. Loader-Spalte: fallunabhängige Suche nach den expliziten Dateinamen ausschließlich in DBManager.js; ein Treffer ist eine Fundstelle, kein Funktionsnachweis. „Kein direkter Treffer“ schließt andere oder dynamische Loader nicht aus. Verzeichnis- und Wildcard-Inhalte wurden für diese Suche nicht expandiert. Tests: Kein dedizierter Test für die jeweilige Auswahl nachgewiesen, außer den unten genannten Teilprüfungen; die Testsammlung wurde nicht vollständig semantisch auditiert.

Der Generator setzt den angekündigten Standard irrtümlich auf date statt cdate, validiert die Eingabe nicht, löscht den bestehenden Client-Baum nicht und überschreibt mit xcopy /C /Y; „Copied“ bestätigt keinen Erfolg.

docs.text:
Die ausgewählte Additions-WorldMap-Tabelle (worldviewdata_table.lub) und die Renewal-Sprachdatei (worldviewdata_language.lub) der gepinnten Revision 680a2f2126c8eb5872bf06cf441685c408ed1358 passen im Rohzustand nicht vollständig zusammen: Die sechs Schlüssel MSI_102_CH1_FILD1, MSI_2_CH1_ZERO1 bis MSI_2_CH1_ZERO4 und MSI_DUN51 wurden im Upstream zwar mit dem 2025-08-02-Update (d336ab454031fda5868e710cbf2435216474bff4 / 8e71824234385c7cd5084ccbd6976c8dbeb44019) eingeführt, beim Übertragen der erweiterten worldviewdata_table.lub nach Additions/ (a2e9b9dd94511a345a730faad9fa988f182a8fa2) jedoch nicht in Translation/Renewal/.../worldviewdata_language.lub übernommen. Die tatsächliche Darstellung im Client hängt weiterhin auch von den geladenen GRFs ab.

images/remote/tests/check-roenglish-generator.php prüft mit synthetischen Fixtures unter anderem sechs Texttabellen, stateicon/efstids, stateiconimginfo, worldviewdata_table, Cash-Shop-Banner, die ItemDBNameTbl-Grenze und ein .gat-Beispiel. images/remote/tests/check-roenglish.py vergleicht ausgewählte Additions-Dateien; images/remote/tests/check-roenglish.sh prüft PetEvolution mit Lua; scripts/py/check-compose.py prüft unter anderem die PetEvolution-Weiterleitung. Die aktuelle CI-Konfiguration führt diese vorhandenen Generator-Fixtures, die Übersetzungsprüfung einschließlich check-roenglish.py und den Compose-Smoke-Test aus, wenn der Scope als relevant erkannt wird. Ein konkretes CI-Laufergebnis wurde für diese Bestandsaufnahme nicht überprüft. Diese Tests belegen keine vollständige Menüäquivalenz oder Client-Laufzeit. images/remote/roenglish-generate.php implementiert eine explizite Teilmenge; dessen all entspricht nicht der vollständigen Batch-Auswahl.

docs.text:
• Im Lua-Gesamtpaket lassen die Pfade für effecttool, skilleffectinfo, stylingshop und CashEmotion lua files aus; Einzelzweige verwenden es. skillinfoz/skillid.lub, stateicon/stateiconinfo.lub (nur Gesamtpaket) und SystemEN/Signboard_C.lub fehlen laut Inventar an den referenzierten Additions-Quellpfaden.
  • monster_size_effect: bis einschließlich 2017-06-14 wird die datierte Quelle auf den normalen Zielnamen kopiert, danach die normale Quelle. Rune wird ab 2023-08-02 kopiert und set_reward.lub vor 2024-10-16 anschließend gelöscht. Die datierten Varianten von PrivateAirplane und EquipmentProperties werden nicht ausgewählt.
  • Das Karten-Gesamtpaket verwendet Wildcards für GAT/GND/RSW und explizite BMPs; der Einzelzweig fordert insbesondere sch_lab.bmp an, das Gesamtpaket nicht. Das Menü nennt zweimal 11; Zweig 12 kopiert mjolnir_11. Maßgeblich für Wildcards, Ordnerinhalte und Bedingungen sind die Batch-Anweisungen und der gepinnte Quellbaum.

docs.title: ROEnglishRE-Addon-Audit
docs.text: Stand: 2026-11-05. Gegenstand ist der vollständige Addons/-Baum von ROEnglishRE 680a2f2126c8eb5872bf06cf441685c408ed1358 und der in Compose gepinnte roBrowserLegacy ed8570e8bbc7ffe1285c82ec7166c01703a73277. Dies ist eine statische Kompatibilitätsprüfung, kein Nachweis eines funktionierenden Spiels. Untersucht wurden alle elf Addon-Verzeichnisse, ihre Dateien, Skripte und die einschlägigen Client-Verbraucher. Quellenpfade in Tabellen sind relativ zum jeweiligen Repository-Root; L bedeutet data/luafiles514/lua files/. Die verlinkten Quellen sind revisionsgebunden.

docs.title: Auswahl und Laufzeit
docs.text:
Compose pinnt beide Revisionen; Overrides der Build-Argumente können andere Quellen wählen. Der Generator akzeptiert bei ROENGLISH_ADDONS ausschließlich compatible, kopiert aber keine Addons. ROENGLISH_ADDITIONS=all ist eine ausdrücklich beschränkte Auswahl aus dem separaten Additions/-Baum, nicht eine Auswahl aller Addons. Basis, optional Pre-Renewal und datumsspezifische Compatibility-Layer werden davor ausgewählt; anschließend folgen ausgewählte Additions und optional Legacy Maps. Details und Einschränkungen stehen im Upstream-Inventar. Eine Auswahl in dieser Matrix ist eine Empfehlung für spätere Arbeit, keine bereits aktive Konfiguration.

loadLua muss für die Lua-Loader eingeschaltet sein. Der RemoteClient bedient generiertes data/ und SystemEN/; für fehlende System/-Dateien gibt es grundsätzlich keinen GRF-Fallback und keinen allgemeinen SystemEN-Alias. Loose-Dateien des Operators werden beim Start überlagert; lokale Browser-GRFs können eine andere Priorität ergeben. Exakte Details: Ressourcenpfade, Startup. Die folgenden Zielpfade sind daher erwartete Client-Pfade, keine Behauptung, dass Dateien heute dort liegen. Groß-/Kleinschreibung, Encoding und vorhandene Daten müssen mit realem Deployment geprüft werden.

Bewertung: „Kandidat“ bedeutet passender Loader und prinzipiell passendes Format, aber keine Freigabe; „teilweise“ bedeutet eine konkrete Einschränkung; „nicht automatisch“ umfasst fehlende Integration oder benötigten Merge. Alle Bewertungen gelten nur für den gepinnten Client und die untersuchten Daten.

docs.title: Tests und Evidenzgrenzen
docs.text:
Die drei Dateien des Stateicon-Patches wurden zusätzlich mit dem gepinnten SystemEN/LuaFiles514/rotp_f.lua unter Lua 5.1 ausgeführt. Der Patch benötigt diese Datei über require() und erzeugte Tabellen mit 1.320 EFST-Einträgen und 847 Statuseinträgen; die verglichene reguläre Renewal-Kombination enthielt 1.315 beziehungsweise 842. Die fünf zusätzlichen IDs 2000 bis 2004 beschreiben Mild-Wind-Varianten und verweisen auf vorhandene Icon-Namen wie i_p_FIRE.tga. Das bestätigt weder die Belegung dieser IDs durch den jeweiligen Server noch das Vorhandensein der TGA-Dateien im verwendeten GRF. Es ist daher kein Nachweis für eine allgemeine automatische Aktivierung des Patch-Satzes.

Die gepinnte Signboard-Legacy-Datei wurde ebenfalls unter Lua 5.1 ausgeführt: Sie erzeugt 625 Einträge. Die ersten sechs Felder haben jeweils die vom roBrowser-Callback erwarteten Typen; bei 102 Einträgen sind zusätzlich Text und Farbe vorhanden. Die gepinnte Pre-Renewal-Tabelle enthält dagegen nur einen Eintrag, der in der Legacy-Tabelle unverändert vorkommt. Damit ist der Parser grundsätzlich ein Kandidat, aber Karten, Koordinaten und referenzierte Assets sind noch nicht gegen ein konkretes Server-/GRF-Paar geprüft. Die vom Client angefragte Großschreibung muss zudem mit dem Vorrang vorhandener loser Dateien zusammenpassen. Die zusätzlichen 624 Einträge enthalten serverabhängige Angaben, etwa einen „Eden Warper“ in prontera bei (124,76) und Level-180-Zugangshinweise in ein_dun02 bei (16,250) und odin_tem03 bei (276,236). Die Datei liefert keine belegte Clientdatumsgrenze. Daher wäre ihre automatische Aktivierung für alle Server und PACKETVER-Werte eine unbelegte Datenentscheidung.

  • Der vollständige Upstream-Baum wurde bei obiger SHA ausgecheckt und die Dateiliste, Readmes, CLS-Auswahl, repräsentative Datenstrukturen und Client-Loader wurden lesend geprüft. Die lokale roBrowser-Revision wurde mit dem Compose-Pin abgeglichen. Der Checkout lag außerhalb des Arbeitsbaums; Forks wurden nicht verändert.
  • Konkrete Negativbefunde sind die oben zitierten Navigationswerte und Verbraucher sowie die tbl-Extraktion statt main(server_name). Dass ein Dateiname geladen wird, beweist weder vollständige Ausführung noch richtige Darstellung.
  • php images/remote/tests/check-roenglish-generator.php wurde bei der ursprünglichen Inventarisierung lokal versucht, konnte aber mangels lokalem PHP nicht starten. Der Fixture-Test lief später in GitHub Actions; er prüft die Generatorauswahl, nicht die Addons im Browser. Abgesehen von den oben beschriebenen Lua-Tests wurden keine Addon-Lua-Läufe, Windows-Patches, HTTP-/GRF-Auflösung oder End-to-End-Spielszenarien getestet. Ein früherer Hinweis im Inventar auf Lua-ladbare Navigation ist hier nicht erneut reproduziert.

docs.title: Umsetzungsvorschläge
docs.text:
1. Pro Datensatz explizite, standardmäßig deaktivierte Auswahl mit Quellen-SHA und Konfliktbericht vorsehen; Basisschicht, Compatibility, Additions, Addons und Operator-Overrides deterministisch dokumentieren. Nie ganze alternative Tabellen ohne Versions- und Serverprüfung freischalten.

  3. Navigation anhand realer Beispieldatensätze und erwarteter Monster-IDs, Karten und Routen testen; gepackte Felder und Distanzformat erst anhand ihrer tatsächlichen Semantik unterstützen. Keine unverbundene Teilmenge über bestehende Tabellen legen.
  4. Für Non-kRO und CLS ein explizites Merge-Modell mit Konfliktdiagnose und Abhängigkeitsreihenfolge entwerfen. Für charserverabhängige Itemdaten die Auswahl im Client explizit implementieren und mit beiden Modi testen; native Patch-Sessions lösen das nicht.
  5. Erst nach bestandenen Tests und geklärten Asset-/Lizenzfragen einzelne Kandidaten in eine konkrete Auswahl übernehmen. Diese Vorschläge wurden nicht implementiert.

docs.title: Other tools and Linux limits
docs.text:
Verified: LuaConverter.bat invokes bundled luac.exe to produce .lub; the executable is a 32-bit Windows PE program. The script also mentions uncompressed .lub files. Tools/msgstringtable/encode.py and Tools/simplemsg/encode.py Base64-encode individual CSV fields into new CSV files. Repute and MacroReport batch wrappers call their jsonbson.py converters; the converters identify py-bson as a dependency. These tools use relative working-directory paths and produce output files when run.

Porting limits: Windows batch commands, xcopy, code page 1252 and the bundled executable are not native Linux equivalents. Linux case-sensitive paths, spaces and legacy encoded non-ASCII path bytes require explicit handling; do not blindly normalize or transcode names. Reproduce or deliberately correct ordered overwrites, mode fallback, deletions, missing sources and menu behavior. Any replacement Lua compiler must match the target runtime's bytecode expectations; a .lub extension alone proves nothing. Nemo/WARP patches, GRF lookup and resource loading are separate from copying files. No native Linux port, Windows execution, generated output comparison or end-to-end client test was performed for this inventory.

docs.title: CI Scope and Test Fixtures
docs.text: CI and security workflows share a data-only source-pin and image-input resolver. Uncertain Git comparisons or malformed pins enable conservative validation and image security work. PR scan aggregation and exact-digest AMD64/ARM64 release gates are unchanged. Script-only tests may reuse a published image only by immutable digest, with an ancestor source revision and unchanged image inputs; unreliable fixtures fail rather than trigger an implicit rebuild. Local override fixtures exclude ignored files, and HTTP smoke-test ports bind to loopback.

docs.title: Bootstrap safeguards
docs.text:
The old unsafe rAthena installer remains disabled without replacement. Its exit-only legacy placeholder was removed after finding no necessary internal caller or documented compatibility requirement. No unsafe alternative was enabled.

Client uploads stage temporary siblings and verify size before atomic per-file replacement. Failed streams preserve existing files; cleanup is best-effort if the API or node is unavailable. Whole-client atomicity and cryptographic content validation are not claimed.

Manual bootstrap requires expected suspended Flux owners and rejects active Kustomizations across namespaces. The old web entrypoint delegates to this same check-only default. Fresh-only MariaDB installation requires explicit chart version, refuses existing Flux/operator infrastructure and aborts missing prerequisites/webhook readiness. Live upgrades or data migration require separate approval and tested recovery; see operations.

Publisher code is pinned to the validated initiating commit. Unchanged unadopted releases use existing digest/source/security-proof journal recovery without unconditional rebuilds. Security gates, human review and permissions are unchanged.

The fork pin updater runs only from the default branch, checks pull requests through the GitHub API before and after candidate validation, and fails closed on API errors. Its 24-hour Dependabot window is a heuristic, not proof of a completed update run; see upstream updates.

docs.title: Image release controls
docs.text:
Main CI gates the existing Container Security workflow. It builds changed remote, robrowser, rAthena and wsProxy candidates for AMD64/ARM64, scans each platform and generates SPDX SBOMs. Publication does not rebuild them: it promotes the exact approved digest and verifies its source SHA/candidate digest. Source must belong to main ancestry; per-component ancestry checks prevent older releases from replacing newer tags even when scan completion order differs. The pre-promotion journal on automation/image-release-state is trusted approval state: restrict writes and do not delete or merge it. The publisher updates one draft PR with blob-SHA compare-and-swap, preserves newer pins, and fails closed on missing proof or API permissions. See publishing protocol for artifact retention, migration, recovery and required-check prerequisites.

The configured Trivy threshold is HIGH/CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed=true, exit-code=1. Fixable findings at that threshold block publishing; lower severities and unfixed findings are not equivalent blocking guarantees. A green result is not proof that every vulnerability is absent. Unchanged images are not rebuilt or rescanned just because a documentation/manifest commit reached main.

Rebuilt components provide sbom-remote, sbom-robrowser, sbom-rathena or sbom-wsproxy artifacts, each containing platform inventories. The ready-component record ties source and digest to promotion. Review the run/artifacts and registry metadata, not just stable. See image provenance.

docs.title: Runtime controls
docs.text:
The project application Deployments retain non-root UID/GID 1000, dropped Linux capabilities, no privilege escalation, runtime-default seccomp and configured probes/resources. MariaDB and infrastructure operators use their own charts/images; do not claim every cluster container uses the application UID. wsProxy also has a readonly root filesystem; frontend/PHP use separate writable runtime paths.

The namespace labels enforce Pod Security baseline and audit/warn restricted. The DB NetworkPolicy allows only the selected game/loader peers and the labeled MariaDB controller in its own namespace on TCP3306. The operator needs SQL access to reconcile Database/User/Grant; do not remove the policy or broadly open ingress as a bootstrap workaround. Client mounts remain readonly to remote.

Vite restricts DNS hostnames to the configured HOST and disables CORS; this does not replace network isolation or authentication. Several workloads still need writable root filesystems. Harden them only after identifying and testing every required writable path. The rAthena entrypoint retains compatibility defaults for credentials; supply unique credentials. The MariaDB client receives its password through MYSQL_PWD, which may be visible to processes with access to its environment; restrict process access.

Remote and roBrowser fetch pinned sources in build stages and do not include Git in their runtime images. roBrowser retains npm and its locked development dependencies for the existing in-image CI tests.

Both Compose game stacks pass explicitly selected environment variables to each service. Their entrypoints reject empty database or interserver passwords; MariaDB rejects initialization without a root password. Hercules uses MYSQL_PWD for database initialization and removes it before starting the server. Its login server suppresses Info and Notice messages because upstream logs passwords in those categories; this also reduces operational visibility. Restrict access to container environments, generated configuration and the game network. Hercules is scanned in the PR image-security matrix but is not published by the release workflow. A scan and isolated integration test do not establish production safety. The starter's lifecycle commands can render without credentials. The standalone MariaDB installer renders private Secret files and includes interserver credentials; it still changes cluster resources and must only be run with explicit approval. The shared Flux base retains the historical host until the separately reviewed second migration stage. Runtime integration and release security scans remain required before deployment.

docs.title: PHP branch and request-time hardening
docs.text:
images/remote/Dockerfile requires php84 >=8.4.27 and a build-time/runtime guard rejects PHP >=8.5 or older 8.4 packages. On Alpine 3.24 the generic CLI explicitly links to php84; Apache uses its PHP8.4 module. security.ini disables session upload progress before request parsing. TRACE/Git-path blocking and the pinned RemoteClient .htaccess remain tested. The frontend image has no Apache/PHP, and remote does not fetch the frontend tree or Node/npm.

The no-cache remote candidate build reruns Alpine package installation; apk's --no-cache alone is not Docker layer-cache invalidation. There is no scheduled PHP-package rebuild or general CI workflow_dispatch release path. New packages do not update an existing container automatically; an approved source/build change must pass the normal release/image-pin chain.

A scoped read-only diagnostic after an approved rollout can check:

kubectl -n ragnarok exec deployment/remote -- php -v
kubectl -n ragnarok exec deployment/remote -- php -r 'echo get_cfg_var("session.upload_progress.enabled"), PHP_EOL;'

Expect PHP in the permitted 8.4 branch and upload progress 0. Do not weaken checks or restart an old image and call it a security update.

docs.title: Secrets and local files
docs.text:
K3s setup requires a locally supplied installer and trusted SHA-256; review the installer and its downloaded artifacts separately. Flux bootstrap requires an explicit confirmation and may commit and push to GitHub. Existing installations are inspected without automatic repair. Never log tokens or kubeconfig contents.

.env, client files and unversioned overrides are local configuration, not CI inputs automatically copied to GHCR. Keep actual credentials outside Git. The bootstrap uses the supplied .env values exactly; it does not silently generate or rotate passwords. Review template defaults before production use.

The private offline bootstrap renderer requires the operator-owned configuration, writes owner-only output and refuses overwrites. Database and interserver credentials are Secret fields; ConfigMaps contain non-secret settings only. Default --check and fake-API tests perform no installation. --apply is a separately approved cluster-changing operation and never deletes namespaces/resumes Flux. The legacy standalone rAthena installer is disabled; it previously exposed interserver credentials in a ConfigMap and interpolated them into SQL.

Use SSH/credential helpers for Git authentication rather than embedding tokens in remote URLs. Do not print .git/config, git remote -v, kubeconfigs, Secret values, full environments or private bootstrap JSON in public logs. Even a URL inspection can expose a token. Redact browser/HMR token queries from diagnostics. If a credential appears in output, revoke/replace it; deleting a local log does not revoke it or remove every copy.

The upstream updater's UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN belongs in Actions Secrets, with the minimum repository-scoped Contents/Pull requests permissions required. GitHub secret scanning, push protection and branch rules are external repository settings; verify them separately rather than assuming this Markdown enforces them. Their presence does not make leaked credentials safe or rotate them.

docs.title: Updates and recovery
docs.text:
Dependencies/base images/actions are pinned as described in upstream updates. Source/dependency PRs require human review, separately from draft GitOps image release approval. Active Flux adopts merged manifests automatically; it must be coordinated during emergency imperative work. Dependabot security updates are independent of the scheduled version-update group; review them promptly. Configured security groups are limited to one ecosystem; grouping across directories also depends on repository or organization settings. Docker image vulnerabilities still require the existing image scans; Dependabot does not provide Docker security PRs.

Do not use setup scripts, namespace resets, blanket image/containerd pruning or PVC/Longhorn deletion to fix an application incident. Keep private rollback and backup material, but never commit it. Follow operations and separately reviewed DB/storage recovery procedures.

docs.title: Upstream source updates and release automation
docs.text: build/dependencies.env pins the roBrowserLegacy, RemoteClient-PHP, rAthena and ROEnglishRE forks. A fork sync does not itself change a deployed image. Check Fork Updates runs daily and supports manual dispatch. It compares the configured repository HEADs, updates changed pins together and validates the candidate source layouts.

docs.title: Dependency update cycle
docs.text:
Dependabot checks npm overlays, Dockerfiles and GitHub Actions in one multi-ecosystem version-update group on Mondays at 12:00 Europe/Berlin. GitHub may omit incompatible updates or create additional PRs when grouping is not possible; inspect the Dependabot logs and review the complete diff. Security updates are separate from version updates and are not held for this schedule. GitHub groups security updates only within an ecosystem; review and merge urgent security PRs promptly, independently of the regular cycle. npm and GitHub Actions have explicit security groups; grouping across npm directories additionally depends on the repository or organization setting. Dependabot security updates were enabled at the 2026-11-09 review; verify that grouping setting separately. Docker does not support Dependabot security updates, so retain the existing image security scans.

The updater waits at least 24 hours after Monday 12:00 Europe/Berlin and checks all open Dependabot PRs targeting main before proposing pins. Open version PRs block the update; PRs explicitly labeled security do not. An unlabeled security PR is conservatively treated as a version PR and can delay the pin PR. The daily retry also handles weeks with no version PR and cycles that take longer to review. The updater checks again after layout validation and skips if main changed. It creates at most one pin PR per weekly cycle, or updates an existing pin PR once per cycle. A cycle marker in the PR body prevents another update or PR in the same cycle; do not remove it. Later fork changes wait for the next cycle. Fork synchronization remains independent and is not performed by this workflow. An operator can also dispatch the same guarded check on main:

gh workflow run dependency-update.yml --repo raiken-mf/robrowser_docker --ref main

It creates or updates one PR containing all changed fork HEAD pins, not one PR per dependency. Review the exact commits, upstream compatibility and required validate check before merging. The updater does not sync forks itself and does not update the Hercules pin; handle Hercules separately when explicitly needed. GitHub does not expose a reliable completion event for the scheduled Dependabot run: the 24-hour window is a heuristic, not proof that a delayed or failed run finished. A PR opened after the final check can still race with pin creation. Review Dependabot logs and the pin PR before merging; security updates remain independent and should be reviewed promptly.

At the time of the 2026-11-09 review there were no open PRs. After enabling the group, inspect open Dependabot PRs and alerts again: merge urgent security fixes independently, and review or close superseded regular PRs only after confirming their updates are included in the new group. Do not close unresolved security PRs merely to reduce PR count. Verify the group in Insights > Dependency graph > Dependabot after the configuration reaches the default branch and inspect the first scheduled run. See GitHub's multi-ecosystem configuration and security update documentation.

docs.title: Distinct approval boundaries
docs.text:
• The source updater uses UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN to create/update automation/upstream-dependency-update. It force-pushes that dedicated branch only with a lease against the observed remote revision.
  • Dependabot checks actions, image bases and the project npm overlays. Neither workflow requests auto-merge; human review and branch protection remain required.
  • Dependabot PRs must receive the required validate check. If GitHub requires approval for a workflow run, an authorized maintainer must approve it; do not bypass the check or execute untrusted PR code with elevated permissions.
  • These are source/dependency PR behaviors. Publish opens a separate draft GitOps image-pin PR, and does not request its auto-merge. It requires release approval before an active Flux reconciler adopts it.

Repository rules and externally configured automation must also be checked for unintended bypasses; these workflows cannot enforce repository settings.

The updater requires a repository-scoped UPSTREAM_PR_TOKEN with Contents and Pull requests write access. Keep it in Actions Secrets, never Git or chat. A workflow rerun retains its original source SHA; do not replay an old publishing run to release newer main or bypass the publication freshness/security gates.

docs.title: Validation and publication
docs.text:
CI validates the pinned Dockerfile-required source layout, API override parity, Compose/templates, translations, runtime isolation and frontend modules. Changed main candidates pass both platform scans and SBOM generation before exact-digest promotion. Main ancestry and recorded component approvals determine publication order even when main advances during scans; a newer approved release is not downgraded. Unchanged image components retain their existing release tags.

roBrowserLegacy changes affect the frontend robrowser image. RemoteClient and ROEnglishRE changes affect remote. rAthena and wsProxy are separate images. The project-owned frontend package/lockfile supplies dependencies required by the pinned source, including granny-ro-js; update it deliberately when necessary. The API HTML/module override must be reviewed if upstream initialization changes.

Only after approving/merging the generated image-pin PR does active Flux adopt the changed release. See GitOps lifecycle and image provenance. Layout/module/CI checks do not prove all gameplay/content compatibility. The completed installation's successful login does not close unrelated graphics, Lua or GRF-content issues.

docs.title: Confirmed operating baseline
docs.text:

  • K3s on Raspberry Pi and Longhorn working.

Documentation-only merges may advance Flux source/applied revisions without changing application specifications. No infrastructure setup, Kubernetes deployment, Flux action or storage operation was performed during that cleanup.

docs.title: Repeatable tests
docs.text:
See development for the local/CI commands and operations for live read-only checks. The existing PR validate gate is scope-sensitive: documentation-only changes can pass without image builds. A strict MkDocs build and local link checks are the relevant documentation validation.

The final documentation cleanup runs offline bootstrap fixture/protocol tests, syntax/Kustomize checks and a strict documentation build. It does not claim those commands execute a new real cluster installation. Future installation examples must be reviewed against the target context and current external scripts.

docs.title: Scope intentionally left open
docs.text:
The rAthena multi-stage image built and passed entrypoint checks on local ARM64 for Renewal and Pre-Renewal. Two local AMD64 builds under emulation failed with compiler segmentation faults at different compilation steps. The cause is not established; the AMD64 build and entrypoint tests must pass on a native GitHub runner before merging. Local ARM64 results do not establish AMD64 compatibility.

Graphics, Lua, GRF-content and other client/gameplay errors are separate tasks. Do not hide them by weakening security/readiness checks or resetting a working namespace/database. Capture sanitized browser/server diagnostics and use a separately reviewed fix when that work is authorized.
